title: Ordinal sign sequences and their numerical order
notes: A number is a map from a well-ordered set to the two arrows \(\uparrow,\downarrow\); unequal numbers are compared lexicographically. The tree includes \(0,\uparrow,\uparrow\downarrow\).
statement: Work in a class theory such as NBG. A surreal is a function \(s:\alpha\to\{-,+\}\), with \(\alpha\) an ordinal. Identify well-ordered domains by their order type. At the first differing position compare with \(-<\text{undefined}<+\). This gives a total order on the proper class \(\mathbf{No}\); the empty sequence is zero.
reconstruction: The undefined-sign convention and passage from an arbitrary well-order to its ordinal order type are supplied explicitly.
fate: Conway's construction predates the talk (book 1976; Knuth's exposition 1974). The sign-sequence theorem and its order are explicitly recorded in \citet[\S2.1]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}; the early book is \citet{conway1976numbers}. The supplied alias 1977-445.1 is the same source occurrence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Simplicity, truncations and the canonical cut
notes: \(x\) is earlier than \(y\) when it lies on the path from zero to \(y\). The symbols \(y]\), \(y\rfloor\), \(y\rceil\) denote earlier numbers, respectively all, smaller, and greater. Theorem~2 writes \(x=\{x\rfloor:x\rceil\}\).
statement: Write \(a<_s x\) when \(a\) is a proper initial segment of \(x\). Set \(L_s(x)=\{a<_s x:a<x\}\) and \(R_s(x)=\{a<_s x:a>x\}\). Then \(x=\{L_s(x)\mid R_s(x)\}\), the simplest number strictly between these two sets. Both option sets are sets, although \(\mathbf{No}\) is a proper class.
fate: This is the canonical-cut theorem, already in Conway; \citet[Thm.~2.1(3), Def.~2.2]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes} gives the precise modern statement. Alias 1977-445.2 represents duplicated material.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: The simplest separator of two sets
notes: For sets \(A,B\) with \(a<b\) for every \(a\in A,b\in B\), Theorem~1 asserts a number between them and a unique earliest such number, proved by transfinite induction.
statement: For sets \(A,B\subset\mathbf{No}\), possibly empty, with \(A<B\), the class \(\{x:A<x<B\}\) has a unique simplest member \(\{A\mid B\}\). In particular it has unique minimal sign-sequence length. The claim is not extended to arbitrary proper-class cuts.
fate: \citet[Thm.~2.1(1)]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes} states the exact existence theorem; it is part of the pre-1978 Conway theory. The previous index's 1977-445.3 is a source overlap.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Recursive addition
notes: The definition is \(x+y=\{x\rfloor+y,x+y\rfloor:x\rceil+y,x+y\rceil\}\).
statement:
For canonical options of \(x,y\), define recursively
\[x+y=\{x^L+y,\ x+y^L\mid x^R+y,\ x+y^R\}.\]
Each family ranges over its entire option set. Induction on the well-founded product of the two simplicity orders makes the recursion well-defined.
fate: The ordered-group construction is in \citet[Chap.~1]{conway1976numbers}, and the formula is reproduced in \citet[Thm.~2.3]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}. Alias 1977-445.4 covers this same page.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Additive identities, order and sign reversal
notes: The notes prove \(0+0=0\), \(x+0=x\), assert commutativity and associativity, and obtain the opposite by reversing arrows. A sentence calls the sum the simplest operation monotone in each argument.
statement: The operation makes \((\mathbf{No},+,0,<)\) an ordered abelian group: \(x+0=x\), \(x+y=y+x\), \((x+y)+z=x+(y+z)\), and \(x+(-x)=0\). Negation interchanges the two signs at every position. Translation preserves strict order. Simplicity characterizes the recursive cut, not an arbitrary pointwise monotone binary function.
reconstruction: The dubious handwritten symbol in the associative-law display is read mathematically as a plus. The informal monotonicity sentence is restricted to its recursive context.
fate: These are the standard field-operation theorems of \citet[Chap.~1]{conway1976numbers}; compare \citet[Thm.~2.3 and the following uniformity paragraph]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Two arithmetic exercises
notes: The exercises ask \(\uparrow\downarrow+\uparrow\downarrow=?\) and \(\widehat{\uparrow}+\downarrow\downarrow\downarrow=?\).
statement: In sign notation \(+-=1/2\), hence \((+-)+(+-)=1\). With \(+^\omega=\omega\) and \(---=-3\), the second answer is \(\omega-3=+^\omega---\). These are exercise questions, not unresolved conjectures.
fate: They follow directly from the recursive group law and the ordinal embedding, already established in \citet[Chaps.~1--2]{conway1976numbers}; \citet[\S2.1]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes} gives the conventions used here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: The basic multiplication inequality
notes: For \(r<s\), \(u<v\), the overwritten sign in \(ru+sv\mathrel{?}rv+su\) resembles \(>\).
statement:
In an ordered field, if \(r<s\) and \(u<v\), then
\[ru+sv-rv-su=(s-r)(v-u)>0.\]
Thus the correct strict sign is \(>\). Positivity of \(r,s,u,v\) is not needed.
fate: This is an elementary ordered-field identity underlying Conway's multiplication. Its role in the recursive product is described in \citet[\S2.2]{mantovamatusinski2017survey}; the displayed factorization independently checks the sign.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: The four-family product cut
notes: The notebook gives four expressions: same-side options on the left of the cut and opposite-side options on the right.
statement:
For canonical surreal options, let \(P(a,b)=ay+xb-ab\). Then
\[xy=\{P(x^L,y^L),P(x^R,y^R)\mid P(x^L,y^R),P(x^R,y^L)\}.\]
All indicated pairs of options are included. The induction uses smaller arguments, and the inequalities follow from the signs of \((x-a)(y-b)\).
fate: This is precisely Conway's product, known before the talk; see \citet[Chap.~1]{conway1976numbers} and \citet[Thm.~2.3]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Ring laws and the multiplicative identities
notes: The notes derive \(x\cdot0=0\) and \(x\cdot1=x\), and assign associativity, commutativity and distributivity as homework.
statement: For all surreals \(x,y,z\), the recursive operations satisfy \(xy=yx\), \((xy)z=x(yz)\), \(x(y+z)=xy+xz\), \(x0=0\) and \(x1=x\), with \(1=\{0\mid\varnothing\}\).
fate: The established ordered-field theorem is the exact match: \citet[Chap.~1]{conway1976numbers}, restated in \citet[Thm.~2.3]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}. A request to prove these facts at home is not a research problem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Uniformity: independence of a cut representation
notes: The advice is to prove addition is ``bracket indifferent'': if \(x=\{a:b\}\), \(y=\{c:d\}\), use \(\{a+y,x+c:b+y,x+d\}\). The same property is claimed for multiplication.
statement: For any set presentations \(x=\{A\mid B\}\), \(y=\{C\mid D\}\) as simplest cuts, the usual addition and multiplication formulas remain valid with options from \(A,B,C,D\), even when these are not the canonical options. The value is independent of the presentation.
reconstruction: The singleton-looking letters in the notes are treated as generic members of option sets; the claim is not invariance under arbitrary changes of inequalities.
fate: This is uniformity of the Conway operations, explicitly distinguished from associativity in \citet[paragraph after Thm.~2.3]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}; it was already part of \citet[Chap.~1]{conway1976numbers}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: An infinite number and its reciprocal infinitesimal
notes: \(\omega=\widehat{\uparrow}\), \(\varepsilon=\uparrow\widehat{\downarrow}\), \(\omega\varepsilon=1\), and \(\omega+\varepsilon=\widehat{\uparrow}\uparrow\widehat{\downarrow}\).
statement: The sign sequences \(+^\omega\) and \(+-^\omega\) represent \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{-1}=\{0\mid2^{-n}:n\in\mathbb N\}\). Their product is one. The sum has \(\omega+1\) plus signs followed by \(\omega\) minus signs; equivalently its normal form is \(\omega+\omega^{-1}\). Here hats indicate an \(\omega\)-long block, not an ordinal exponentiation rule.
reconstruction: The lengths of the repeated sign blocks are made explicit; the notation is interpreted as concatenation.
fate: Conway's infinite arithmetic predates 1978. The product calculation is written out in \citet[\S2.2, example before Thm.~2.6]{mantovamatusinski2017survey}; the normal-form theorem is also in \citet[Thm.~2.4]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Ordinals and Hessenberg natural arithmetic
notes: Ordinals have only up arrows. Ordinary ordinal addition is noncommutative; the note names ``Hessenburg'' and says his natural addition and multiplication coincide with surreal arithmetic.
statement: The embedding \(\alpha\mapsto+^\alpha\) sends ordinal natural sum and natural product to surreal addition and multiplication. For Cantor normal forms, natural addition adds coefficients of equal powers and natural multiplication distributes with natural sums of exponents. Ordinal concatenation instead satisfies \(1+_{\rm ord}\omega=\omega\ne\omega+_{\rm ord}1\).
fate: \citet[Chap.~2]{conway1976numbers} treats the ordinal embedding; \citet[\S2.1, end]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes} explicitly identifies the induced operations as natural sum and product. The surname is Hessenberg.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Division and positive square roots
notes: Every nonzero number has \(1/x\); \(y/x\) exists; every \(x>0\) has \(\sqrt{x}\), by transfinite induction.
statement: For every nonzero surreal \(x\), there is a unique \(y\) with \(xy=1\). Every positive surreal has a unique positive square root. These are assertions about a proper-class real-closed ordered field, with the usual finite algebraic formulas.
fate: The field and real-closedness results were already established by Conway; see \citet[Chaps.~1, 4]{conway1976numbers}. \citet[Thm.~2.3]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes} states the combined theorem precisely.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Polynomial intermediate values do not eliminate gaps
notes: A polynomial taking opposite signs at two points has a zero between them; nevertheless there are gaps, for example between finite and infinite numbers. A class-long arrow is said no longer to be a surreal.
statement: If \(p\in\mathbf{No}[T]\) has finite degree and \(a<b\) satisfy \(p(a)p(b)<0\), some \(c\in(a,b)\) satisfies \(p(c)=0\). This does not imply Dedekind completeness. The cut with all finite surreals on the left and all positive infinite surreals on the right is unfilled: a finite candidate can be increased by one, and a positive infinite candidate can be halved. There is no ordinal-length sign sequence with proper-class domain.
reconstruction: Finite degree, the coefficient field, and the precise finite/infinite cut are supplied. The sentence is not a denial of polynomial order-continuity.
fate: Polynomial intermediate values follow from the pre-existing real-closedness theorem, \citet[Chap.~4]{conway1976numbers}; \citet[Thm.~2.3]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes} verifies the relevant algebraic hypothesis. The gap argument is supplied here to disambiguate ``without continuity''.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Periodic signs and two rational examples
notes: The notebook records \(\widehat{\uparrow\downarrow}=2/3\) and \(\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow=3/4\).
statement: The finite sequence \(+-+\) denotes \(3/4\). The \(\omega\)-long alternating sequence \(+-+-\cdots\) denotes \(2/3\): its finite truncations alternate about \(1-1/2+1/4-\cdots=2/3\), and their cuts determine that real number.
fate: These are examples of the real embedding in Conway's theory, \citet[Chap.~2]{conway1976numbers}; compare the sign representation of real numbers in \citet[\S2.1]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}. No new irrationality or summation question is posed.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Exponentiation, logarithms and real-base powers
notes: The notes say that \(\exp x\), \(x^y\) and \(\log\) exist, then begin a recursive construction.
statement: The Kruskal--Gonshor exponential is an order-preserving group isomorphism \(\exp:(\mathbf{No},+)\to(\mathbf{No}_{>0},\cdot)\), agreeing with the real exponential. Its inverse is \(\log\). For \(x>0\) define \(x^y=\exp(y\log x)\). This power operation must be distinguished from the normal-form monomial map \(a\mapsto\omega^a\).
reconstruction: Positivity of the base and the distinction between ordinary powers and the monomial map are supplied.
fate: \citet[Introduction]{gonshor1986surreal} dates his first exposure to Kruskal's ideas to January 1977; Chap.~10, published in 1986, develops exponentiation from Kruskal's hints. Thus B records subsequent development by Gonshor, not discovery in this particular 1978 talk or publication soon afterward. The exact map is stated in \citet[Thm.~2.7]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the exponential ordered-field structure is established. The notebook does not specify a new open problem about it.

title: Exponential growth beyond every fixed polynomial
notes: For positive infinite \(x\), \(2^x>x^n\) ``for any \(n\).
statement: If \(x\in\mathbf{No}\) exceeds every real number and \(n\in\mathbb N\) is fixed, then \(\exp(x\log2)>x^n\). The quantifier is over ordinary finite integers, not arbitrary surreal exponents: taking \(n=x\) would reverse the inequality when \(x>2\).
reconstruction: The range of n is restricted to ordinary finite integers.
fate: This is an established property of the Kruskal--Gonshor exponential; \citet[Chap.~10]{gonshor1986surreal} is the definitive later treatment. \citet[\S2.3]{costinehrlich2024integration} states that \((\mathbf{No},\exp)\) is an elementary extension of the real exponential field, which yields the stated fixed-integer inequality.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, established for finite polynomial degree. The unrestricted exponent reading is false.

title: The exponential series at an infinitesimal
notes: For infinitesimal \(x\), \(\exp x=\sum_{n\in\text{finite}}x^n/n!\).
statement:
For \(|\varepsilon|<1/n\) for every positive integer \(n\),
\[\exp(\varepsilon)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon^n/n!,\]
where the sum is Hahn/Conway summation of normal forms. It is not a claim that ordinary sequence convergence in the full order topology is sufficient.
reconstruction: The summation sense and starting index zero are supplied.
fate: The local analytic construction is part of Conway's pre-1978 power-series calculus; its agreement with the global exponential is \citet[Chap.~10]{gonshor1986surreal} and \citet[Prop.~8(ii)]{costinehrlich2024integration}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Arbitrary real-coefficient power series at infinitesimals
notes: The line reads ``\(x\) infinitesimal, \(n\) real'' followed by \(\sum x^n a_n\) convergent for all \(a_n\); the placement of the coefficient qualifier is doubtful.
statement: For a sequence \((a_n)_{n\ge0}\) of real coefficients and a surreal infinitesimal \(\varepsilon\), the family \((a_n\varepsilon^n)_{n\ge0}\) is summable in Conway's normal-form sense. No analytic radius of convergence is required. Neither arbitrary real-indexed sums nor arbitrary surreal coefficients satisfy this assertion without extra summability hypotheses.
reconstruction: The intended reading is \(a_n\) real and \(n\) a nonnegative integer; this is a mathematical reconstruction, not a claimed certain paleographic correction.
fate: \citet[Chap.~4, p.~40]{conway1976numbers} is the pre-talk result. It is stated verbatim mathematically as a formal-power-series theorem in \citet[Prop.~4]{costinehrlich2024integration}. For a counterexample to unrestricted coefficients, choose nonzero \(\varepsilon\) and \(a_n=\varepsilon^{-n}\): every term is one.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Asymptotic integration and an incorrect Gaussian formula
notes: A possible application is written \(\int_x^{\text{class-long }\uparrow}e^{-\xi^2}\,d\xi=\sum n!/x^n\). The scan confirms the Gaussian exponent and the displayed factorial series; no scale factor or alternating signs are visible.
statement:
For real \(x>0\), the corrected classical expansion is
\[\int_x^\infty e^{-t^2}\,dt\sim\frac{e^{-x^2}}{2x}\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{(-1)^n(2n-1)!!}{2^n x^{2n}}.\]
At a positive infinite surreal argument, substitution of \(x^{-1}\) makes the formal power series summable; an equality to a surreal integral additionally requires a specified extension and integration operator. The factorial series in the notebook is not that Gaussian expansion.
reconstruction: The corrected Gaussian asymptotic series is our explicit mathematical repair. It does not recover an unwritten 1978 definition of the integral.
fate: The broader asymptotic-integration method was subsequently developed by \citet[Defs.~68, 76; Thms.~78, 85]{costinehrlich2024integration}: preprint 30 August 2022, revised July 2024, journal 2024. Their result concerns a specified class of resurgent functions and their extensions, not all smooth functions; \S13 gives foundational obstructions to broader constructive operators. This is a partial match to the proposed method, not a proof of the literal formula.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the specified resurgent integration theory is developed. The notebook leaves no precise function-class or axiomatic open problem; no new problem-index entry is manufactured. A complete finite-remainder check is supplied in the critical annotations.

title: Omnific integers and an insufficient truncation criterion
notes: The notes write \(\widehat{\uparrow}\downarrow=\omega-1\) and \(|x]-x|=1\) as the definition of an integer.
statement: The relevant integers are the omnific integers \(\mathbf{Oz}\), equivalently the surreals \(z=\{z-1\mid z+1\}\). In normal form they have no negative exponents and the coefficient at exponent zero is an ordinary integer. The formula with an arbitrary earlier truncation is not an equivalent criterion: for \(x=3\), its truncation zero has distance three.
reconstruction: The Oz interpretation is required by the adjacent quotient theorem. The notes do not say which truncation, if any, should be selected.
fate: Omnific integers were already treated in \citet[Chap.~5]{conway1976numbers}. The book's opened excerpt is insufficient to recheck this chapter directly; the quotient assertion is independently verified from the stated normal-form characterization in the critical annotations, and the historical attribution remains indirect.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: Every surreal is a quotient of omnific integers
notes: \ru{Всякое число} is a ratio \(m/n\) of two integers.
statement: For every \(x\in\mathbf{No}\), there exist \(m,n\in\mathbf{Oz}\), \(n\ne0\), with \(x=m/n\). Indeed choose a positive surreal \(a\) exceeding the negatives of every exponent in the set-sized support of the normal form of \(x\). Then \(n=\omega^a\) and \(m=\omega^a x\) have only positive exponents and are omnific integers. For zero use \(0/1\). The assertion with ordinary integers is false.
reconstruction: The qualifier omnific is supplied from the theory; it is essential. The short proof is an independent verification of the intended assertion.
fate: This is the field-of-fractions result of Conway's \emph{Number Theory in the Land of Oz}, \citet[Chap.~5]{conway1976numbers}; the normal-form theorem needed for the displayed verification is read in \citet[Thm.~2.4]{kuhlmannmatusinski2015classes}. No claim of novelty is attached to the proof.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is an established part of surreal arithmetic under the hypotheses stated above; no open problem is asserted here.

title: The unfinished recursive exponential cut
notes:
The last formula starts
\[\exp x=\{0,\exp x]\sum_{m=1}^n(x-x])^m/m!:\exp x]/\sum_{m=0}^n(x]-x)^m/m!\]
with no final brace and undifferentiated earlier options.
statement: A valid full recursive definition must separate left and right options, include the constant term in Taylor polynomials \(E_n(t)=\sum_{m=0}^nt^m/m!\), and retain only positive reciprocal denominators. The Kruskal--Gonshor construction uses two families on each side of the cut, besides zero, and yields the exponential of item 1978-446.16. The printed two-family fragment is not a standalone total definition.
reconstruction: Completion requires more than closing delimiters. The canonical modern construction is identified separately, without silently inserting it into the diplomatic transcript.
fate: The complete formula is given in \citet[Chap.~10]{gonshor1986surreal} and \citet[\S2.3, recursive exponential definition]{mantovamatusinski2017survey}. This is a partial mathematical match: no claim is made that the missing terms were actually spoken. For example, at \(x=1\), the earlier option zero and \(n=1\) give a reciprocal denominator \(E_1(-1)=0\) in the unqualified notebook rule.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the completed Kruskal--Gonshor construction is established; the literal notebook recursion remains incomplete.

title: A two-dimensional matrix lattice action
notes: The notes take \(g_x\in GL(n,\mathbb R)\), \(S=\operatorname{Tr}\sum_{x,\delta}g_x^{-1}g_{x+\delta}\), and write \(\sum_\delta(g_{x+\delta}g_x^{-1}-g_xg_{x-\delta}^{-1})=0\).
statement: On a finite two-dimensional lattice with periodic boundary conditions, or with variations supported away from its boundary, vary each invertible matrix by \(\delta g_x=\epsilon_xg_x\). Stationarity of the displayed oriented nearest-neighbour action is equivalent to \(\sum_\delta(A_{x\delta}-A_{x-\delta,\delta})=0\), where \(A_{x\delta}=g_{x+\delta}g_x^{-1}\). The two positive lattice directions are summed. This is an algebraic Euler--Lagrange identity; positivity of the action is not asserted for \(GL(n,\mathbb R)\).
reconstruction: The finite-lattice or compact-support condition makes the variation legitimate. It is not stated in the notebook. The action and its equation can be verified directly without assuming integrability.
fate: The continuum principal-chiral-field setting was already in print in \citet[\S2]{zakharovmikhailov1978relativistic}, submitted 4 January 1978. That is a partial model match, not a citation proving the exact fully discrete action integrable.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The variational identity is valid. The stronger integrability assertion is assessed separately.

title: Complete integrability and higher discrete currents
notes: The system is called completely integrable, with an \(L,A\)-pair and infinitely many currents satisfying \(\sum_\delta(J^{(k)}_{x\delta}-J^{(k)}_{x-\delta,\delta})=0\). The first current is \(A\); the second ends after \(\varepsilon_{\delta\gamma}A_{x\gamma}+\).
statement: The first conservation law is exactly the preceding lattice field equation. A complete theorem for higher currents would have to specify the remainder in \(J^{(2)}\), the recursion, boundary conditions, and the meaning of independence or completeness of the conserved quantities. Those data are absent.
reconstruction: No missing second-current term is invented. The semi-discrete matrix Toda result below and the continuum principal chiral field do not by themselves prove the fully discrete assertion.
fate: \citet[\S2]{zakharovmikhailov1978relativistic} treats the continuum model, while \citet[\S1 and \S9]{takebezabrodin2025multicomponent} treats matrix Toda hierarchies. Neither checked passage identifies the unfinished current for precisely this lattice action.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The first current is established; the claimed complete hierarchy is not identifiable from the surviving formula. This is an unresolved identification, not evidence that a precise open problem remains.

title: The semi-discrete nonabelian Toda chain
notes: With \(A_s=g_s^{-1}\dot g_s\), \(B_s=g_s^{-1}g_{s+1}\), the equations are \(\dot B_s=-A_sB_s+B_sA_{s+1}\), \(\dot A_s=B_s-B_{s-1}\). A kinetic term is written \(\dot g_s^{-1}\dot g_s\), without parentheses or a factor \(1/2\).
statement: Let \(g_s(t)\in GL(n,\mathbb C)\) be twice differentiable, with a finite periodic chain or locally finite variations. The first equation follows identically from the definitions. The second is the nonabelian Toda equation \(\frac{d}{dt}(g_s^{-1}\dot g_s)=g_s^{-1}g_{s+1}-g_{s-1}^{-1}g_s\). A compatible Lagrangian is \(\sum_s\operatorname{Tr}(\tfrac12 A_s^2-B_s)\). For \(n=1\), \(g_s=e^{q_s}\) gives \(\ddot q_s=e^{q_{s+1}-q_s}-e^{q_s-q_{s-1}}\).
reconstruction: The normalized Lagrangian is a reconstruction. Interpreting the notebook literally as \(\frac{d}{dt}(g_s^{-1})\dot g_s\) gives \(-A_s^2\), not the stated kinetic normalization.
fate: \citet[\S1, equation (1.3), references 34 and 45, and \S9]{takebezabrodin2025multicomponent} explicitly attributes the unpublished matrix Toda equation and its integrals to Polyakov, and records Krichever’s 1981 periodic/quasiperiodic solution theory and Korepin’s 1981 Hamiltonian quantization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The matrix Toda system is an established integrable hierarchy. The scalar reduction and the displayed first-order system are precise; the notebook Lagrangian needs normalization.

title: A spectral zero-curvature representation for matrix Toda
notes: The explicit request is to find \(L_s(A,B,\lambda)\), \(M_s(A,B,\lambda)\) such that \(\dot L_s+M_sL_s-L_sM_{s+1}=0\) is equivalent to the Toda equations.
statement: For the matrix Toda system, construct a spectral auxiliary linear system whose compatibility yields both first-order equations. One concrete realization uses the spectral equation for the block Jacobi operator \(\mathcal L=E^{-1}+A+BE\), with \((Ef)_s=f_{s+1}\), and time evolution generated by \(\mathcal M=BE\); compatibility is \(\dot{\mathcal L}=[\mathcal M,\mathcal L]\). Rewriting its second-order difference equation as a first-order block system gives a transfer-matrix representation, with a convention-dependent sign in the time equation.
reconstruction: The distinction between transfer matrices and difference operators is added. The notebook uses \(L_s\) for both, although their zero-curvature equations are not literally identical.
fate: The matrix Toda solution theory is explicitly traced to Krichever’s 1981 work in \citet[\S1 and \S9]{takebezabrodin2025multicomponent}. The operator calculation here also verifies directly the requested compatibility at the formal algebraic level.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The Lax-representation problem is resolved; analytic spectral theory depends on finite, periodic, or infinite-chain boundary conditions.

title: Conservation of a transfer product and its endpoint terms
notes: The notebook writes \(\frac{d}{dt}\prod_{s=-\infty}^{\infty}L_s=0\) and calls the product a generating function of integrals; its diagram omits endpoint transport.
statement: For finitely many ordered matrices satisfying \(\dot L_s=L_sM_{s+1}-M_sL_s\), the product \(T_{a,b}=L_a\cdots L_b\) satisfies \(\dot T_{a,b}=T_{a,b}M_{b+1}-M_aT_{a,b}\). If the endpoint matrices vanish, \(T\) is constant. If they agree, \(T\) evolves by conjugation and \(\operatorname{Tr}(T^k)\) is constant. An infinite product additionally needs convergence, a normalization, and control of the endpoint limit.
reconstruction: The telescoping identity supplies the missing hypotheses; equality of endpoint matrices alone does not make the matrix product constant.
fate: The analogous monodromy mechanism already appears in the inverse-scattering framework of \citet[\S\S1--2]{zakharovmikhailov1978relativistic}. The particular endpoint identity is checked algebraically here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The unconditional equality is false; its conserved-spectrum version is standard and valid under the stated conditions.

title: A formal matrix Riccati recursion and conserved coefficients
notes: The proposed recursion is \(L_s=1+\lambda A_s-\lambda^2B_sL_{s+1}^{-1}\). Expanding its ordered product produces \(\sum_s A_s\) and \(\sum_{s<s^{\prime}}A_sA_{s^{\prime}}-\sum_sB_s\); the latter is called a nontrivial integral.
statement: In formal power series with constant term the identity, the recursion determines coefficients successively: \(L_s=I+\lambda A_s-\lambda^2B_s+O(\lambda^3)\). For a finite product in increasing \(s\), its coefficient of \(\lambda^2\) is exactly the displayed ordered expression. Conservation of a coefficient follows only when the associated product is conserved, or after taking conjugacy-invariant functions in the periodic case. An infinite-chain coefficient requires summability or subtraction of a background.
reconstruction: Formal-power-series interpretation, remainder terms, ordering, and the distinction between matrix coefficients and scalar invariants are supplied.
fate: This belongs to the matrix Toda construction subsequently developed by others; see \citet[\S1 and \S9]{takebezabrodin2025multicomponent}. The two coefficients are directly checkable, but the checked source does not establish the notebook’s exact recursion with its boundary normalization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The displayed low-order expansion is correct after reinstating remainder terms; unqualified infinite-product conservation is not.

title: The block Jacobi Lax equation
notes: Equation (14) gives \(L=E^{-1}+A_s+B_sE\), \(M=B_sE\), where \(E\) shifts by one site.
statement: In the algebra of matrix-valued difference operators, use \(EC_s=C_{s+1}E\). Then \([BE,E^{-1}+A+BE]=(B_s-B_{s-1})+(B_sA_{s+1}-A_sB_s)E\). Thus \(\dot L=[M,L]\) is equivalent to the two matrix Toda equations. For a finite periodic block matrix, all coefficients of its characteristic polynomial are conserved.
reconstruction: The commutator equation and finite periodic consequence are made explicit. For an infinite operator, isospectrality requires a suitable operator domain and well-posed evolution.
fate: The identification with nonabelian Toda is supported by \citet[\S1 and \S9]{takebezabrodin2025multicomponent}; the complete formal commutator calculation is elementary and included in the statement.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The algebraic equivalence is established. No infinite-dimensional spectral theorem is inferred from the formal identity alone.

title: Lattice curvature and the continuum Yang--Mills action
notes: A link matrix \(B_{x\alpha}\) is attached to each positive edge. The plaquette is \(F_{x\alpha\beta}=B_{x\alpha}B_{x+\alpha,\beta}B^{-1}_{x+\beta,\alpha}B^{-1}_{x\beta}\); the trace sum is said to tend to \(F^2\).

For a compact unitary gauge group, a real Wilson action using \(\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(I-F_{x\alpha\beta})\), with the appropriate power of \(a\) and normalization, tends to the positive curvature-square action. A raw trace sum differs by a constant, sign, and normalization and is not automatically real.
reconstruction: The mesh scaling and the compact-unitary reality convention repair the shorthand. The exponential expansion on the page is a truncation, not an exact identity.
fate: \citet[\S\S II--III]{wilson1974confinement} introduced the gauge-invariant plaquette lattice action in 1974; the original paper and the continuum-limit discussion were checked.

title: The lattice Yang--Mills equation as a sum of plaquette differences
notes: For fixed \(\alpha\), neighbouring plaquettes in the \(\alpha\beta\) planes are subtracted and summed over \(\beta\). In the expanded second plaquette, its first inverse has index \(x,\beta\).
statement: Varying a link in a trace plaquette action gives a sum of neighbouring oriented plaquettes, all based at the same vertex; for a constrained gauge group the result is projected to its Lie algebra. The inverse edge leaving \(x\) in the negative \(\beta\) direction is \(B^{-1}_{x-\beta,\beta}\), not \(B^{-1}_{x,\beta}\). With this correction the second product closes and the continuum equation is \(D_\beta F_{\alpha\beta}=0\), up to the chosen sign of curvature.

title: Based holonomy and curvature insertions
notes: \(\Psi(C_y)\) is the ordered product of links along a based contour. Attaching a small square compares \(\Psi(C+\Pi)\Psi(C)^{-1}\) with a curvature transported to the base point.
statement: For a smooth matrix connection and a piecewise smooth based loop, holonomy transforms by conjugation at the base point. Inserting a sufficiently small oriented plaquette at a point reached by transport \(U\) changes the holonomy, to first order in its area, by \(UF_{\alpha\beta}U^{-1}\) in the corresponding left or right logarithmic derivative. Taking a trace removes dependence on the base-point frame. Matrix holonomy itself is not a gauge-invariant scalar.

title: The principal chiral field and a spectral flat connection
notes: As a finite-dimensional analogue, \(A_\mu=g^{-1}\partial_\mu g\) and \((\partial_\mu+z\varepsilon_{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu)\phi=A_\mu\phi\) lead to a formula with denominator \(1-z^2\).

title: Flat holonomy and spectral integrals of the chiral model
notes: Flatness is used to write a closed-contour ordered exponential as 1 and to infer conservation of the transport along a spatial line.
statement: A flat connection has trivial holonomy around contractible loops in its domain; noncontractible loops can have nontrivial monodromy. Transport along a spatial interval evolves by endpoint multiplication. On a periodic spatial circle its conjugacy class is conserved; on a line, a normalized scattering matrix is constant under suitable decay and endpoint normalization. Expanding conjugacy-invariant spectral functions then gives conserved quantities.

present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Valid with the stated topology and boundary hypotheses; false if read as trivial holonomy of every flat connection.

title: The massive Green-function analogy

Changing the operator sign changes the source normalization. The notebook records the exponential rate and suppresses the dimension-dependent prefactor.

title: Projected areas as contour coordinates
notes: The contour tensor is \(\sigma_{\alpha\beta}=\oint_C x_\alpha\,dx_\beta\). Its functional derivative is written using \(\delta_{\mu\alpha}x^{\prime}_\beta-\delta_{\mu\beta}x^{\prime}_\alpha\).
statement: For a closed \(C^1\) loop in \(\mathbb R^4\), \(\sigma_{\beta\alpha}=-\sigma_{\alpha\beta}\). For a smooth periodic variation \(h\), \(D\sigma_{\alpha\beta}[h]=\int(h_\alpha x^{\prime}_\beta-h_\beta x^{\prime}_\alpha)\,ds\). These six oriented projected areas are translation invariant and insensitive to reparametrization preserving orientation. By Stokes’ theorem they are integrals of the constant two-forms \(dx_\alpha\wedge dx_\beta\) over any spanning surface.
reconstruction: The differentiability and closure hypotheses, independent antisymmetric components, and orientation convention are explicit additions.

title: Reduction to area variables and self-dual momentum
notes: Assuming \(G\) depends only on \(\sigma\), the notes replace contour derivatives by derivatives \(\pi_{\alpha\beta}=\partial/\partial\sigma_{\alpha\beta}\), require their quadratic contraction to be scalar, and invoke \(\pi=\pm{}^{*}\pi\).

With a fixed orientation, its two-form is either self-dual or anti-self-dual. The Hodge convention is \(({*}P)_{\alpha\beta}=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}P_{\gamma\delta}\). This finite-dimensional fact does not by itself classify solutions of a differential system in six area variables.

title: Self-dual area profiles and the Hamilton--Jacobi identity
notes: The proposed area expression is \((\sigma^2\pm\sigma{*}\sigma)^{1/2}\), and the notes say it solves \(|\delta A/\delta x(s)|^2=|x^{\prime}(s)|^2\).

At \(\sigma_\pm\ne0\), the derivative is pairing with the constant two-form \(\omega=\sqrt2\,\sigma_\pm/|\sigma_\pm|\), which has comass one and corresponds to an orthogonal complex structure \(J\). Consequently the contour gradient is \(Jx^{\prime}\), up to orientation convention, and its norm equals \(|x^{\prime}|\). The functional is nondifferentiable at \(\sigma_\pm=0\).

title: Gauge degeneracy of the Yang--Mills action
notes: The action is \(S(A)=\int\langle F_{\mu\nu},F^{\mu\nu}\rangle dV\), with \(F=dA+A\wedge A\), and gauge transformation \(A^g=gAg^{-1}+g\,dg^{-1}\). The Lorenz condition \(\partial_\mu A_\mu=0\) is given as a gauge condition.

The change of variables from an orbit parameter and slice coordinates produces a determinant \(\Delta_f=|\det(df\circ T_x)|\), with chosen measures. title: The orbit-volume determinant in a finite-dimensional quotient
notes:
For a free isometric action the notebook writes
\[\int_M e^{-S}=\int_{M/G}e^{-S}\det(TT^*)^{1/2}dV,\]
with \(T:\mathfrak g\to T_xM\). No prime or group-volume factor is visible.
statement: Let a compact Lie group act freely and isometrically on a Riemannian manifold, and choose an Ad-invariant inner product on \(\mathfrak g\). For an invariant integrable function \(h\), the quotient integration formula is \(\int_Mh\,dV_M=\operatorname{vol}(G)\int_{M/G}h\sqrt{\det(T_x^*T_x)}\,dV_{M/G}\), with Haar volume defined by that inner product. Equivalently use the nonzero determinant of \(T_xT_x^*\). The full latter operator is singular whenever the quotient has positive dimension.
reconstruction: The determinant is moved to the injective operator on \(\mathfrak g\), or replaced by a nonzero determinant. Normalizing Haar volume to one absorbs the explicit group-volume constant.
fate: This is the finite-dimensional quotient construction underlying the already published degenerate-Gaussian discussion \citep[metadata]{schwarz1978partition}. The correction follows from singular-value decomposition and the coarea formula; it is not an attribution to an unread theorem in that paper.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The notebook formula is false with the ordinary determinant on \(T_xM\); the corrected density is standard.

title: Degenerate Gaussian integrals and analytic torsion
notes: The mathematical theory for quadratic actions and an application to Ray--Singer invariants are announced, without a torsion formula.

In an elliptic complex on a closed manifold, zeta-regularized alternating Laplacian determinants define analytic torsion, with treatment of cohomology required if zero modes are present. The notebook records this connection, not a new proof of metric independence.

title: Semiclassical integration over a critical manifold
notes: The problem is the small-parameter asymptotic of \(\int e^{-S/\alpha}\), with a manifold of stationary points and strong degeneracy. The proposed answer integrates a determinant over instantons.
statement: On a compact Riemannian manifold without boundary, suppose the minimum set \(N\) is a compact smooth submanifold and the Hessian of \(S\) is positive definite in its normal bundle. For Riemannian volume, the leading Laplace term is \(e^{-S(N)/\alpha}(2\pi\alpha)^{(\dim M-\dim N)/2}\int_N(\det H_\perp)^{-1/2}dV_N\). Gauge directions must first be quotiented or fixed. The field-theory version replaces the determinant by a regularized nonzero determinant and introduces collective-coordinate zero modes.
reconstruction: The finite-dimensional Morse--Bott hypotheses clarify the heuristic. An arbitrary stationary point, saddle, or noncompact critical family does not satisfy this formula without further analysis.
fate: The instanton-sector realization is given in \citet[\S2, equation (2.5)]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum}; that paper explicitly identifies its central result as announced in 1978.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The finite-dimensional formula is standard. Its sigma-model use is a controlled formal one-loop calculation after the specified regularizations, not a general path-integral theorem.

title: Dimension of the SU(2) instanton family
notes: The shorthand says that for every \(q\) there is a family of \(8q-3\) instantons, besides infinite-dimensional gauge symmetry.
statement: For charge \(q\ge1\), the unframed moduli space of smooth anti-self-dual \(SU(2)\) connections on the round four-sphere, modulo gauge, has real dimension \(8q-3\). The framed problem on \(\mathbb R^4\) has dimension \(8q\). The integer describes parameters, not a count of solutions. Orientation conventions interchange self-duality and anti-self-duality.
reconstruction: The base, framing, positivity of charge, and meaning of the dimension are supplied; the zero-charge case is not covered by the written expression.
fate: \citet[abstract and theorem, pp. 2662--2663]{atiyahhitchinsinger1977deformations} established the dimension in 1977. The primary abstract was read, but the scanned-paper link yielded only a download-preparation page. The earlier cumulative entry reports a reading of both pages; that reading was not repeated here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: This is established prior instanton moduli theory, not a new 1978 assertion.

title: Rational maps as sphere-valued instantons
notes: For \(n:\mathbb R^2\to S^2\), stereographic projection gives \(w(z)\), and the notes say extremals correspond to rational functions, crediting Belavin and Polyakov.
statement: For smooth finite-action maps extending across infinity to \(S^2\), the positive-degree energy-minimizing instantons are holomorphic maps \(S^2\to\mathbb{CP}^1\), hence rational functions of degree \(q\). Negative-degree anti-instantons are antiholomorphic; constant maps give degree zero. Thus the unqualified phrase all extremals are rational in \(z\) omits the opposite orientation. No claim is made here about arbitrary noncompact-domain or singular stationary maps.
reconstruction: The claim is restricted to its instanton setting, and the antiholomorphic sector is restored. Finite action and extension at infinity are essential.
fate: The prior Belavin--Polyakov construction is explicitly restated and credited in \citet[\S1, equations (1.6)--(1.8)]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum}. The original 1975 PDF link could not be opened, so the attribution is verified indirectly through this primary paper.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The rational-map instanton classification is established; the notebook suppresses the anti-instanton sector.

title: The sigma-model topological bound
notes: The action splits into \(c_1N+c_2\int |\partial_{\bar z}w|^2/(1+|w|^2)^2\); the measure and constants are suppressed.
statement: For \(n:S^2\to S^2\), or a smooth finite-energy map on \(\mathbb R^2\) with constant value at infinity, define \(q=(4\pi)^{-1}\int n\cdot(\partial_1n\times\partial_2n)\,d^2x\). Then \(\int|dn|^2\,d^2x\ge8\pi|q|\). Equality holds for the appropriate first-order conformality equation, equivalently a holomorphic or antiholomorphic stereographic map. With the notebook action \(S=f_0^{-1}\int|dn|^2\), the bound is \(8\pi|q|/f_0\).
reconstruction: The factor reflects the absence of \(1/2\) in the notebook action. The signed decomposition uses the sign of \(q\), and \(d^2x\) must be included.
fate: The completed-square argument is read in \citet[\S1, equation (1.6)]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum}, where the earlier Belavin--Polyakov work is cited.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The topological bound is standard and sharp under the stated finite-action conditions.

title: The instanton Hessian as a Dolbeault Laplacian
notes: The fluctuation bundle is pulled back from \(T\mathbb{CP}^1\), and \(\Delta=\bar\partial^*\bar\partial\). For fixed degree, \(\bar\partial\) is said to be the same and the metric depends on \(w\).
statement: For a degree-\(q\) holomorphic map \(w:S^2\to\mathbb{CP}^1\), the complex tangent fluctuation line bundle is \(w^*T\mathbb{CP}^1\cong\mathcal O(2q)\). The second variation at the instanton is, up to normalization, the nonnegative Dolbeault Laplacian on its sections. Holomorphic line bundles of the same degree on \(S^2\) are isomorphic, so one can fix a holomorphic model while varying its Hermitian metric. Its complex kernel has dimension \(2q+1\), or real dimension \(4q+2\).
reconstruction: The compactified domain and infrared regulator are restored. A bare-plane differential operator does not automatically have the compact discrete spectrum used in the next step.
fate: \citet[\S2, including equations (2.5)--(2.8), and \S3]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum} gives the regulated fluctuation calculation and counts its zero modes. The calculation extends work already announced in 1978.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established elliptic and instanton-moduli description. The identification of holomorphic structures requires a choice of isomorphism.

title: Zeta-regularized nonzero determinants
notes: The notes define \(\zeta(s)=\sum_{\lambda_i\ne0}\lambda_i^{-s}\) and \(\log\det=-\zeta^{\prime}(0)\), saying that zero is a regular point.
statement: For a nonnegative self-adjoint elliptic differential operator of positive order on a smooth closed compact manifold, remove its finite-dimensional kernel. Its spectral zeta function is initially defined for large real part, continues meromorphically, and is regular at zero; set \(\det{}^{\prime}_{\zeta}\Delta=\exp[-\zeta_\Delta^{\prime}(0)]\). For a noncompact domain, a relative determinant, boundary/infrared regularization, or other definition is required.
reconstruction: The ellipticity, positivity, compactness, and zero-mode exclusion are stated explicitly. The determinant is of the positive fluctuation operator, not an arbitrary first-order operator without a spectral cut.
fate: The construction predates the lecture: \citet[\S1, equations (1.5)--(1.6)]{raysinger1971torsion} uses the same zeta regularity and determinant principle. \citet[Appendix B]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum} applies it to the instanton computation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An established regularization with precise spectral hypotheses.

title: Metric variation and the Frullani determinant formula
notes: For a fixed differential operator \(A\) with varying adjoint, the notes posit \(\dot{(A^*A)}=BA^*A+A^*CA\), quote Frullani’s identity, then write a positive heat integral for \(\log\det A\).
statement: For positive real \(a,b\), \(\int_0^\infty(e^{-ta}-e^{-tb})\,dt/t=\log(b/a)\). Hence a determinant ratio for positive finite-dimensional operators uses a minus sign in front of the corresponding difference of heat traces. For \(\Delta=A^*A\), a regularized heat representation of \(\log\det{}^{\prime}_{\zeta}\Delta\) also has this sign, removes zero modes, and includes the finite-part convention dictated by the Mellin transform. A determinant of \(|A|\) is half that logarithm.
reconstruction: The signs of \(B,C\) depend on the convention for the metric derivative; the displayed variation identity can be taken as their definition. The later positive integral is a separate faithful error and also conflates \(A\) with \(A^*A\).
fate: The exact regulated counterpart is read in \citet[\S2, equation (2.10), and Appendix B]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum}; the heat determinant method was already standard before the lecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Frullani’s identity is correct. The notebook heat-integral sign and unspecified zero-mode subtraction require correction.

title: Variation of the heat trace and local coefficients
notes: Equation (22) puts \(t\partial_t\) only on the \(B\)-trace and adds an un-differentiated \(C\)-trace. The constant heat coefficient is then singled out.
statement: Whenever the relevant compositions are trace class and differentiation is justified, \(\dot\Delta=B\Delta+A^*CA\) implies \(\partial_u\operatorname{Tr}e^{-t\Delta}=t\partial_t\{\operatorname{Tr}(Be^{-tA^*A})+\operatorname{Tr}(Ce^{-tAA^*})\}\). Both summands carry \(t\partial_t\). After dividing by \(t\) and integrating with the determinant sign and zero-mode subtraction, the small-time local coefficients and the large-time kernel projections control the variation.
reconstruction: The missing derivative is confirmed by the source PNG and by cyclicity of trace using \(Ae^{-tA^*A}=e^{-tAA^*}A\). No full determinant is determined by a single local coefficient without normalization and zero-mode data.
fate: \citet[\S3, equations (3.1)--(3.3)]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum} provides the appropriate metric-variation calculation; the general heat-variation machinery is already in \citet[\S6]{raysinger1971torsion}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected trace identity is valid. Its literal notebook version is false.

title: Zero modes and the instanton moduli measure
notes: The \(4q+2\)-dimensional metric determinant on rational maps must be included, and the notes say that its unresolved part cancels the unresolved zero-mode contribution to the fluctuation determinant.
statement: In the regulated degree-\(q\) sector, choose real collective coordinates \(\gamma^a\) for the rational maps and their zero modes \(v_a=\partial n/\partial\gamma^a\). The induced volume has density \(\sqrt{\det(\langle v_a,v_b\rangle)}\,d\gamma\). Combined with \((\det{}^{\prime}\Delta)^{-1/2}\), the variation of this Gram determinant cancels the kernel-projector contribution in the determinant variation, leaving the local anomaly and an overall normalization.
reconstruction: Cancellation is a statement about the combined density and a specified regulator, not permission to drop all zero modes from both calculations.
fate: \citet[\S2, equation (2.7), and \S3]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum} gives the calculation; its central measure result was announced in Frolov--Schwarz 1978, as explicitly recorded in \S1 and reference 13.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The one-loop instanton measure mechanism is identified and established within its regularized semiclassical setting.

title: The zeros-and-poles instanton measure
notes: Writing \(w=c\prod_i(z-a_i)/\prod_i(z-b_i)\), the notebook displays same-sign squared distances above unlike-sign squared distances, and \((1+|c^2|)^{-2}\). The lower product has a free \(j\).
statement: On the chart of degree-\(q\) rational maps with distinct finite zeros and poles and finite nonzero value \(c\) at infinity, the one-loop measure has, up to its regulator-dependent fugacity and overall constant, density \[\frac{1}{(q!)^2}\frac{\prod_{i<j}|a_i-a_j|^2|b_i-b_j|^2}{\prod_{i,j}|a_i-b_j|^2}\frac{d^2c}{(1+|c|^2)^2}\prod_i d^2a_i\,d^2b_i.\] Short-distance collisions require the stated ultraviolet prescription; other rational-map charts cover infinity and degenerations.
reconstruction: The missing product ranges, coordinate differentials, permutation factors, and sector fugacity are supplied from the published formula. Since \(|c^2|=|c|^2\), moving the square outside the modulus does not constitute a mathematical correction.
fate: This exact structural density is \citet[\S1, equation (1.9), and \S3, equation (3.10)]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum}. The authors state that its proof had been sketched in Frolov--Schwarz 1978; the full paper was received 24 January 1979 and published in July 1979.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The formula is an established one-loop density on the instanton sector, with its ultraviolet and infrared restrictions.

title: The neutral two-component Coulomb gas
notes: The denominator of the normalized instanton sum is identified with a Coulomb-gas partition function: poles carry positive charges, zeros negative charges.
statement: Taking logarithms of the zeros-and-poles density gives pair interactions proportional to \(-q_iq_j\log|z_i-z_j|\), with \(q_i=\pm1\), equal numbers of each sign, and the inverse-temperature/coupling product fixed by the exponent 2. A sector sum introduces a fugacity. The collision singularities and infinite-volume limit need a cutoff or a specified renormalized prescription; the measure is not a finite gas partition function without them.
reconstruction: The sign labelling is conventional; exchanging both species leaves the density unchanged. The mapping applies to the semiclassical instanton ensemble described here.
fate: The Coulomb-gas interpretation is developed in \citet[\S4]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum}, whose central instanton measure was already announced in 1978.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The algebraic mapping is established. It does not identify the entire interacting sigma model with this gas.

title: The free-fermion value of the Coulomb-gas coupling
notes: At one temperature, identified parenthetically as the temperature occurring here, the gas is said to be equivalent to free fermions.
statement: For the two-dimensional neutral logarithmic gas at the coupling encoded by squared Cauchy determinants, the identity \(\det(1/(a_i-b_j))\) converts the same-sign/unlike-sign product into a fermionic determinant. With consistent regulators and fugacity, the resulting grand partition function and suitable correlations admit a free-fermion representation. The claim concerns this gas representation of a one-loop instanton ensemble, not an exact equivalence of all sigma-model observables to a free field.
reconstruction: The Cauchy-determinant condition supplies the missing normalization of temperature. A coupling quoted numerically would depend on the convention for logarithmic potential.
fate: The free-fermion treatment is explicit in \citet[\S4]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum}; its references identify the earlier bosonization/free-fermion machinery.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established with the stated sector and regularization qualifications.

title: Rational auxiliary systems and zero curvature
notes: The auxiliary equations are \(\Psi_\xi=U\Psi\), \(\Psi_\eta=V\Psi\), with \(U=U_0+\sum_{n=1}^{N_1}U_n/(\lambda-\lambda_n)\), \(V=V_0+\sum_{m=1}^{N_2}V_m/(\lambda-\mu_m)\). All poles are fixed, simple, pairwise distinct, and the two pole sets are disjoint. Equation (3) instead prints \(U_\xi-V_\eta+[U,V]=0\).
statement: For smooth matrix coefficients on a simply connected coordinate domain and an invertible fundamental solution away from the poles, compatibility of the stated auxiliary equations is \(U_\eta-V_\xi+[U,V]=0\). Conversely, this flatness identity gives a local fundamental solution at each regular spectral parameter. The distinct-pole assumptions define the general-position family considered in the lecture; they are not a definition of every integrable system.
reconstruction: The derivatives in equation (3) are interchanged. The corrected convention is fixed by differentiating the two auxiliary equations, rather than by guessing from later formulas.
fate: The rational family appears in \citet[equations (1)--(2)]{zakharovmikhailov1980variational}. Its receipt line is 3 October 1978, preceding the 27 November lecture; this establishes an earlier manuscript, not the date of first public circulation. The rational family was published by the speakers in 1980.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected compatibility identity is established and the publication match is exact at the level of the rational ansatz.
speaker: V. E. Zakharov

title: A common pole and polynomial Lax pairs
notes: For a Lax pair, the notes describe a simple pole of \(U\) and an arbitrary-order pole of \(V\) at the same point, then write \(U=U_0+U\lambda\), \(V=P_n(\lambda)\).
statement: If rational matrix functions on the spectral sphere have no pole except a common point, a fractional-linear spectral change taking that point to infinity makes them polynomials. Their degrees are the corresponding pole orders. Thus a simple pole for \(U\) and order \(n\) for \(V\) give degree at most one and at most \(n\). This is a subclass of Lax representations, lying outside the disjoint-pole hypothesis above.
reconstruction: The spectral-sphere and no-other-poles conditions are supplied. The statement is not interpreted as a classification of all Lax pairs.
fate: \citet[opening discussion following equations (1)--(2)]{zakharovmikhailov1980variational} separates the generic rational family from familiar degenerations. The polynomial assertion is elementary complex analysis.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Valid under the stated pole hypotheses; the notebook suppresses the change of spectral coordinate.
speaker: V. E. Zakharov

title: Coefficient equations at the poles
notes: Equation (4) gives the flatness of \((U_0,V_0)\), followed by \(U_{n\eta}=[U_n,A_n]\), \(V_{m\xi}=[V_m,B_m]\), where \(A_n=V(\lambda_n)\), \(B_m=U(\mu_m)\).
statement: With the auxiliary-equation convention fixed above, equality of the constant term and all residues is equivalent to \[U_{0\eta}-V_{0\xi}+[U_0,V_0]=0,\qquad U_{n\eta}=[A_n,U_n],\qquad V_{m\xi}=[B_m,V_m].\] The evaluations are finite because the pole sets are disjoint. The two residue commutators in the notebook have the opposite order.
reconstruction: The signs are determined by residue extraction from \(U_\eta-V_\xi+[U,V]=0\). No change of commutator convention is made between equations.
fate: The coefficient system is the starting reduction in \citet[equations (2)--(4)]{zakharovmikhailov1980variational}, received before the lecture and published in 1980; the first public circulation date was not verified. The residue calculation independently checks the signs.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected system is equivalent to zero curvature; the literal notebook signs are inconsistent with its own auxiliary equations.
speaker: V. E. Zakharov

title: Conjugacy orbits and one-variable residue data
notes: The residues are written \(U_n=\varphi_nU_n^{(0)}\varphi_n^{-1}\), \(V_m=\psi_mV_m^{(0)}\psi_m^{-1}\), with \(U_n^{(0)}\) depending only on \(\xi\) and \(V_m^{(0)}\) only on \(\eta\). These matrices are regarded as prescribed Jordan forms.
statement: An equation \(U_\eta=[A,U]\) transports \(U\) by conjugation along \(\eta\); its characteristic polynomial and Jordan type are constant on each such curve. Locally on a stratum where smooth conjugating frames exist, choose representatives \(a_n(\xi)\), \(b_m(\eta)\) and write \(U_n=\varphi_na_n\varphi_n^{-1}\), \(V_m=\psi_mb_m\psi_m^{-1}\). Right multiplication of a frame by an element centralizing its representative changes no residue.
reconstruction: Local smooth frames and constant Jordan type are required; a globally smooth choice of Jordan normal form is not automatic through eigenvalue collisions.
fate: The orbit parametrization and its stabilizer freedom are explicit in \citet[equations (6)--(8)]{zakharovmikhailov1980variational}; its manuscript receipt preceded the lecture, while first public circulation was not established.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The local conjugacy reduction is established. Global gauge charts and singular orbit strata require additional treatment.
speaker: V. E. Zakharov

title: Gauge freedom and equations for the frames
notes: With \(\nabla_\eta=\partial_\eta-V_0\), \(\nabla_\xi=\partial_\xi-U_0\), equation (9) gives linear-looking equations for \(\varphi_n,\psi_m\), with the residues themselves expressed through these frames.
statement: Flatness of \((U_0,V_0)\) permits a local gauge in which \(U_0=V_0=0\). The residue equations then allow representatives satisfying \[\partial_\eta\varphi_n=\left(\sum_m\frac{V_m}{\lambda_n-\mu_m}\right)\varphi_n,\qquad \partial_\xi\psi_m=\left(\sum_n\frac{U_n}{\mu_m-\lambda_n}\right)\psi_m.\] For arbitrary frames there are extra right-hand terms in their centralizers; these can be removed locally by the allowed frame changes.
reconstruction: The passage from commutator equations to frame equations fixes stabilizer gauge. The resulting coupled equations are nonlinear, even though each equation is linear in its own frame when the other residues are held fixed.
fate: \citet[equations (5)--(9)]{zakharovmikhailov1980variational} records the gauge and stabilizer construction in the manuscript received 3 October 1978 and published in 1980; receipt alone does not establish a public preprint date.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The local gauge construction is established; no global triviality is inferred for a multiply connected base.
speaker: V. E. Zakharov

title: The orbit-variable variational principle
notes: Equation (10) displays a trace action with two first-order frame terms and a pairwise interaction \(-U_mV_n/(\lambda_m-\mu_n)\), but the summation letters and the displayed equality sign do not form a consistent expression.
statement: In the gauge \(U_0=V_0=0\), with fixed smooth \(a_n(\xi),b_m(\eta)\), set \(U_n=\varphi_na_n\varphi_n^{-1}\), \(V_m=\psi_mb_m\psi_m^{-1}\). Compactly supported variations of the invertible frames in \[S=\int\operatorname{Tr}\left(\sum_n a_n\varphi_n^{-1}\partial_\eta\varphi_n-\sum_m b_m\psi_m^{-1}\partial_\xi\psi_m-\sum_{n,m}\frac{U_nV_m}{\lambda_n-\mu_m}\right)d\xi\,d\eta\] give exactly \(U_{n\eta}=[V(\lambda_n),U_n]\) and \(V_{m\xi}=[U(\mu_m),V_m]\). Frame equations follow after the centralizer gauge choice. On real forms one must also impose the reality conditions making the action real.
reconstruction: This is an explicitly gauge-fixed reconstruction with corrected dummy indices. Varying the frame kinetic term and integrating by parts verifies the commutator signs; the printed equality before the last term is read as a broken continuation, not an additional identity.
fate: The matching action is \citet[equation (10), with equations (5)--(9)]{zakharovmikhailov1980variational}. Both the published result and the receipt date were checked; the latter is not treated as a public-circulation date; OCR does not reliably preserve every symbol in the original formula, so the displayed normalized action is also checked by direct variation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The variational principle is established for the specified generic rational family. It does not assert that every integrable equation admits this exact action without a limiting or reduction argument.
speaker: V. E. Zakharov

title: Formal conservation-law expansions at the poles
notes: The talk claims \(N_1+N_2\) series of conservation laws, one for each pole, and mentions sine--Gordon with poles at \(0\) and \(\infty\).
statement: For a zero-curvature system admitting local formal diagonalization near a spectral pole, the diagonal scalar compatibility equations generate formal conserved densities and fluxes order by order. Distinct, semisimple leading eigenvalues are a standard sufficient genericity condition. Each of the \(N_1+N_2\) poles offers such an expansion. This counts formal expansion sites, not proven independent global Hamiltonians; integrating the densities requires boundary conditions. Familiar sine--Gordon pairs are reductions with singularities at zero and infinity on the spectral sphere.
reconstruction: The notebook supplies neither the densities nor hypotheses for diagonalization. These qualifications make its mechanism precise without claiming a complete set of independent integrals.
fate: The inverse-scattering setting and sine--Gordon reductions predate this meeting \citep[\S\S1--3]{zakharovmikhailov1978relativistic}. The variational rational family was already in the October 1978 manuscript \citep[equations (1)--(2)]{zakharovmikhailov1980variational}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The formal mechanism is standard. The exact independence and analytic convergence of the asserted series are not established in the notes.
speaker: V. E. Zakharov

title: Many Hamiltonian structures for the rational family
notes: The explicit conjecture is that there are many Hamiltonian structures, as for KdV, which is said to have infinitely many.
statement: A definite conjecture would need to specify a phase space, allowable local or nonlocal Poisson brackets, equivalence of brackets, compatibility, and which flows must be Hamiltonian. None of these choices is recorded. Merely multiplying one Poisson bracket by constants would already give an uninformative meaning of many.
reconstruction: The historical motivation is retained, but no quantifier or modern conjecture is inserted in place of the missing specification.
fate: The final paragraph of \citet{zakharovmikhailov1980variational} discusses the Hamiltonian interpretation under reality conditions and leaves uniqueness of the constructed structure as a question at that time. This is a related, more specific formulation, not evidence for a present unsolved problem matching every possible reading of the lecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The precise conjecture cannot be identified. The 1980 question is not promoted to an open claim in 2026 without a defined category and a further literature match.
speaker: V. E. Zakharov

title: Euclidean scalar correlators and renormalization
notes: Lipatov motivates a small coupling by the approximate fine-structure value \(\alpha=e^2/(4\pi\hbar c)\simeq1/137\), then writes the four-dimensional scalar action with \(\lambda_0\varphi^4/4!\), the normalized Euclidean integral of \(\prod_i\varphi(x_i)\), and proposes cutoff-dependent bare mass and coupling to make Green functions finite. His cited source is ZhETF 72, 411 (1977).
statement: At finite volume and an ultraviolet lattice or mode cutoff, a positive quartic coupling defines an ordinary finite-dimensional normalized integral. Its moments are full Schwinger functions; connected functions are their cumulants. Perturbative continuum renormalization in four dimensions requires mass, coupling, and field-strength counterterms, plus a vacuum normalization. Order-by-order renormalized coefficients do not by themselves establish an interacting nonperturbative continuum limit.
reconstruction: The finite cutoff and field-strength counterterm are supplied. The ambiguous subscript \((c)\) cannot turn the displayed full moment into a connected correlator without a cumulant subtraction.
fate: \citet[\S2]{lipatov1977divergence}, received 14 July 1976 and published February 1977, is explicitly named in the notebook and sets up the renormalized perturbative calculation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The perturbative framework is established. The literal unqualified assertion about finite continuum Green functions is stronger than the calculation and is not adopted.
speaker: L. N. Lipatov

title: Momentum invariants, amputation, and the physical mass
notes: The four-point function carries \(\delta(p_1+p_2-p_3-p_4)\), depends on scalar products, and is divided by four propagators to define \(\Gamma\). The free propagator is \((p^2+m^2)^{-1}\), while the physical pole is called \(m_c^2\).
statement: In a translation- and rotation-invariant Euclidean scalar theory, strip the overall momentum delta distribution from the connected four-point function and amputate its four external full propagators. The resulting vertex depends on invariant scalar products, subject to momentum conservation. At zero coupling the two-point function is \((p_E^2+m^2)^{-1}\). A stable one-particle mass produces, after the appropriate analytic continuation, a Euclidean pole at \(p_E^2=-m_{\rm phys}^2\), or a Minkowski pole at \(p_M^2=m_{\rm phys}^2\).
reconstruction: Connectedness and the Euclidean/Minkowski sign distinction are explicit repairs. Amputation alone does not in general define a one-particle-irreducible vertex unless the relevant disconnected and reducible contributions have also been specified.
fate: The Green-function and vertex conventions underlying the calculation are treated in \citet[\S2]{lipatov1977divergence}; the lecture is exposition of that prior perturbative setup.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The kinematic construction is established under the stated invariance and analyticity conditions. The notebook changes signature conventions without saying so.
speaker: L. N. Lipatov

title: Invariant charge and its normalization
notes: The invariant charge is written \(\lambda(p_i)=\lambda_0\Gamma(p_i)\prod_i[G(p_i)/G_0(p_i)]^{1/2}\). The preceding definition of \(\Gamma\) does not divide out its tree coupling.
statement: A renormalized effective quartic coupling is obtained by evaluating an amputated connected vertex at a specified nonexceptional subtraction configuration and including the chosen external-field normalization. If a factor \(\lambda_0\) is written separately, the vertex factor must be normalized to one at tree level; if \(\Gamma\) already includes the tree quartic coupling, that extra factor is omitted. These two conventions cannot be used simultaneously.
reconstruction: The missing tree normalization and subtraction scheme are supplied as alternatives, not silently selected from the incomplete formula. The cancellation of a constant field rescaling is the invariant-charge mechanism.
fate: \citet[\S2, definitions of renormalized coupling and renormalization-group function]{lipatov1977divergence} is the expressly cited prior calculation. The notebook’s exact normalization is only a partial match.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The invariant-charge construction is standard; the literal product has an unresolved extra coupling unless the vertex is renormalized by its tree value.
speaker: L. N. Lipatov

title: The leading-logarithm formula and the Landau limit
notes: The displayed expression is \(\lambda_\mu=\lambda_0/[1+(3\lambda_0/32\pi^2)\log(\Lambda/\mu^2)]\), followed by the claim \(\lambda_\mu\to\infty\) for fixed positive \(\lambda_0\) as \(\Lambda\to\infty\). The same paradox is mentioned for electrodynamics.
statement: Taking the formula on its own terms, with \(\Lambda\) a squared ultraviolet scale, \(\mu>0\), and fixed \(\lambda_0>0\), the limit is zero. Conversely, keeping a positive target \(\lambda_\mu\) fixed gives \(\lambda_0=\lambda_\mu/[1-(3\lambda_\mu/32\pi^2)\log(\Lambda/\mu^2)]\), which becomes singular at a finite cutoff. This is the leading-logarithm zero-charge/Landau-pole tension, not a nonperturbative theorem about all possible ultraviolet completions.
reconstruction: The claimed infinite limit is a faithful notebook error, confirmed against the scan. The inverse relation distinguishes removing the cutoff at fixed bare coupling from fixing the renormalized charge.
fate: This is prior renormalization-group background for the coefficient problem in \citet[\S1--2]{lipatov1977divergence}. Its quoted limiting conclusion is disproved directly by the displayed rational function.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The sign and limit audit is decisive. Neither this scalar leading-log formula nor the brief QED analogy proves a general constructive-field-theory result.
speaker: L. N. Lipatov

title: Large-order coefficients from a functional saddle point
notes: The question is the \(k\to\infty\) behaviour of coefficients in \(\psi(\lambda)=a_2\lambda^2+a_3\lambda^3+\cdots\). Four coefficients are said to be known; the proposed method is Laplace’s method for the continuum integral.
statement: In Lipatov’s regulated, renormalized scalar \(\varphi^4\) calculation with a fixed scheme, extract the order-\(k\) coefficient by a contour integral in the coupling and combine it with the regulated field integral. Rescaling the field exposes a large parameter \(k\); saddles at analytically continued negative quartic coupling yield formal factorial large-order contributions, with collective coordinates and fluctuation determinants determining powers and prefactors. With \(t=\log(\Lambda/\mu^2)\), the derivative \(\psi=d\lambda_\mu/dt\) and the physical-scale derivative \(\beta=d\lambda_\mu/d\log\mu\) obey \(\psi=-\beta/2\) when the cutoff and bare parameters used to define \(\beta\) are fixed.
