title: Strong extensions and equivalence
notes: For two \(G\)-modules \(E,F\), an extension is an exact sequence \(0\to F\to H\to E\to0\). Equivalence fixes the end modules. It is called strong if a section exists as a homomorphism of abelian groups, without requiring \(G\)-equivariance.
statement: For modules over \(\mathbb Z[G]\), restrict attention to extensions split after forgetting the \(G\)-action. A strong extension has a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear section, so \(H\cong F\oplus E\) as abelian groups. Equivalence means a \(G\)-module isomorphism commuting with injection and projection and inducing the identity on \(F\) and \(E\). An equivariant section makes the extension trivial. Over a field every short exact sequence splits as vector spaces, but this is false for general abelian groups.
reconstruction: The relative, underlying-module splitting condition is distinguished from unrestricted \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathbb Z[G]}\). The field case does not justify omitting the condition over \(\mathbb Z\).
fate: This is classical extension theory \citep[Chapters X and XIV]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}. Publisher chapter metadata were checked; the specific degree-one block construction is independently verified in the next item rather than attributed to an unread page.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The definition is standard and unambiguous once the underlying category is fixed.

title: Strong group extensions and first cohomology
notes: The coefficient module is \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(E,F)\), with \(g\cdot u=V_guU_g^{-1}\). A section produces a cocycle; conversely the notebook gives the block matrix with upper-right entry \(f(g)U_g\).
statement: Let \(M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(E,F)\) with the stated action. A cocycle satisfies \(f(gh)=f(g)+g\cdot f(h)\), and a coboundary has the form \(f(g)=g\cdot u-u\). The formula \[\rho_f(g)=\begin{pmatrix}V_g&f(g)U_g\\0&U_g\end{pmatrix}\] defines a group action on \(F\oplus E\) exactly when \(f\) is a cocycle. Changing the section changes \(f\) by a coboundary. Thus equivalence classes of strong extensions are naturally \(H^1(G,M)\), with Baer addition agreeing with cocycle addition.
reconstruction: The normalization of the off-diagonal block and the group action on Hom are made explicit; they can be checked by multiplying two block matrices.
fate: The construction belongs to the classical cohomological extension framework \citep[Chapters X and XIV]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}. The checked publisher record confirms the book and chapters; the exact degree-one equivalence is reconstructed directly from the source formulas.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. It classifies all vector-space extensions over a field, and only underlying-split extensions for arbitrary \(\mathbb Z\)-modules.

title: Lie-algebra extensions and the Chevalley--Eilenberg differential
notes: For representations of \(\mathfrak g\) on \(E,F\), the off-diagonal map is \(f(X)\); the notes give its cocycle equation and write \((df)(X,Y)=f([X,Y])-Xf(Y)+Yf(X)\).
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), put \(M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,F)\) and \(X\cdot u=V_Xu-uU_X\). The block map \(X\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}V_X&f(X)\\0&U_X\end{pmatrix}\) is a representation exactly when \(f([X,Y])=X\cdot f(Y)-Y\cdot f(X)\). Changes of splitting add \(X\mapsto X\cdot u\), giving \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_{U(\mathfrak g)}(E,F)\cong H^1(\mathfrak g,M)\). The notebook differential is the negative of the usual degree-one Chevalley--Eilenberg differential, which has the same kernel.
reconstruction: The action on Hom replaces the ambiguous word commutator when \(E\) and \(F\) differ. Algebraic vector-space splitting imposes no finite-dimensionality assumption on \(E,F\).
fate: The enveloping-algebra interpretation and cochain construction are prior results \citep[Chapter XIII, \S\S1,5,8]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}. The chapter text was opened, including its algebraic setup; the displayed degree-one block verification is elementary.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established. The sign convention for \(d\) is harmless when used consistently.

title: Different infinitesimal characters split an algebraic extension
notes: The lemma states that if \(E\) and \(F\) have different infinitesimal characters, then \(H^1(\mathfrak g,\operatorname{Hom}(E,F))=0\). The next page defines the character by scalar action of the centre of the enveloping algebra.
statement: Let \(E,F\) be \(U(\mathfrak g)\)-modules on which every element of \(Z(U(\mathfrak g))\) acts through algebra characters \(\chi_E,\chi_F\). If these characters differ, choose a central \(z\) with values \(\alpha\ne\beta\). In an extension \(H\), \((z-\alpha)(z-\beta)=0\); the two scalar roots are distinct, so its eigenspaces split \(H\) into invariant submodules. The eigenspace mapping to \(E\) is an equivariant complement to \(F\). Therefore \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(E,F)=0\).
reconstruction: The argument makes the scalar-central-action hypothesis explicit. It uses the centre of the universal enveloping algebra, not merely the centre of the Lie algebra, and does not require \(\mathfrak g\) semisimple.
fate: This is an algebraic separation-of-central-characters lemma in the classical module framework \citep[Chapter XIII, \S1]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}. The splitting argument above verifies it directly; later topological-category caveats do not refute it.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established for the algebraic category under the stated hypotheses. Additional continuity is needed when its polynomial projection is used on a topological representation.

title: Relative first cohomology and extensions split over a subalgebra
notes: The notes say that relative cocycles vanish on \(\mathfrak h\subset\mathfrak g\) and describe \(\mathfrak h\)-trivial extensions. They first write that absolute \(H^1\) is relative \(H^1\), and subsequently place an element-of sign between the two groups.
statement: For a \(\mathfrak g\)-module \(M\), relative degree-one cocycles are ordinary cocycles \(f\) with \(f|_{\mathfrak h}=0\); their \(\mathfrak h\)-equivariance follows from the cocycle identity. Relative coboundaries are \(du\) with \(u\in M^{\mathfrak h}\). The natural map \(H^1(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak h;M)\to H^1(\mathfrak g;M)\) is injective, with image the kernel of restriction to \(H^1(\mathfrak h;M)\). For \(M=\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)\), this image consists precisely of extensions admitting an \(\mathfrak h\)-equivariant section.
reconstruction: The image and relative coboundaries replace the two erroneous literal relations. Injectivity is special to degree one here: if a relative cocycle equals \(du\), its vanishing on \(\mathfrak h\) forces \(u\in M^{\mathfrak h}\).
fate: The relative cochain complex is standard prior theory; a checked modern primary formulation is \citet[\S3, opening definition and equation (10)]{wockel2014topological}. Its warning that higher-degree maps need not be injective reinforces the need to retain the degree-one hypothesis.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established as stated. Equality with absolute cohomology requires additional hypotheses and is false in general, for example when \(\mathfrak h=\mathfrak g\) has nonzero absolute \(H^1\).

title: Continuous cocycles and topologically split extensions
notes: A \(G\)-module is now a topological vector space with continuous action. The first idea uses \(f:G\to\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)\), requiring \((g,e)\mapsto f(g)e\) to be jointly continuous.
statement: For continuous representations on locally convex spaces, restrict to short exact sequences with a continuous linear section and the resulting topological identification \(H\cong F\oplus E\). A crossed homomorphism with jointly continuous evaluation gives a continuous block action, and changes by continuous linear sections give coboundaries. Thus the relevant continuous \(H^1\) classifies these topologically split extensions. An arbitrary topological exact sequence need not admit such a section, and the topology on the Hom coefficient space must be compatible with the chosen evaluation condition.
reconstruction: The continuous-section condition is essential. One may specialize to Banach modules and bounded linear maps, but strong continuity must not silently be replaced by operator-norm continuity.
fate: This is the continuous version of the classical cocycle mechanism, used in the prior unitary cohomology theory \citep[\S0(a)]{delorme1977cohomologie}. The general extension-category distinctions are also documented by \citet[Introduction and \S4]{charfi1980extensions}; its bibliography traces the relevant preprints to before this meeting.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established for the specified split category. The notation \(H^1(G,\operatorname{Hom}(E,F))\) alone does not choose that category.

title: Smooth vectors and their topology
notes: The second idea replaces \(E,F\) by their differentiable-vector spaces \(E_\infty,F_\infty\). The word describing their imperfection is unexplained; the next theorem specializes to \(E=\mathbb C\).
statement: For a continuous representation of a finite-dimensional Lie group on a Fréchet space \(E\), let \(E_\infty\) consist of vectors whose orbit maps are smooth. Give it the Fréchet topology induced by the embedding \(v\mapsto(g\mapsto gv)\) into \(C^\infty(G,E)\), equivalently by seminorms controlling all differentiated orbit maps on compact sets. This is a smooth representation with continuous derived action. Replacing both arguments in Hom by smooth vectors changes the extension category and is not merely a change of notation.
reconstruction: The natural smooth-vector topology is supplied; using the original norm on a dense smooth subspace would lose the stated completeness and continuity properties.
fate: \citet[\S5.1, pages 152--153]{blanc1979cohomologie} defines precisely this space and topology. The smooth-vector construction is prior background. The stronger regularization theorem is assessed separately: the manuscript was received 14 December 1977, revised 27 October 1978, and published in 1979, but no earlier public-release date was verified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The construction is established. The notebook’s isolated qualitative criticism has no independent mathematical content without a specified property.

title: Continuous, smooth-vector, and relative Lie-algebra cohomology
notes: For \(E=\mathbb C\), the displayed theorem is \(H^1(G,F)\cong H^1(G,F_\infty)\cong H^1(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k;F_\infty)\), with arrows attributed respectively to Delorme--Blanc and van Est.
statement: Let \(G\) be a connected finite-dimensional Lie group, \(K\) a maximal compact subgroup, and \(F\) a continuous Fréchet \(G\)-module. With continuous cochains on the group, the natural smooth-vector topology, and the derived action on \(F_\infty\), regularization and differentiation give \[H^1_{\rm cont}(G,F)\cong H^1_{\rm cont}(G,F_\infty)\cong H^1(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k;F_\infty).\] Equivalently one may use smooth group cochains after passing to smooth vectors. If disconnected groups are admitted, \(K\)-equivariance must replace merely \(\mathfrak k\)-equivariance and component-group effects must be retained.
reconstruction: Connectedness, Fréchet completeness, and the cochain topologies are supplied. The assertion concerns first cohomology of a single coefficient module; it does not automatically identify all topological Ext groups between two arbitrary representations.
fate: The regularization theorem is read in \citet[Theorem 5.2, page 153]{blanc1979cohomologie}; the notebook attributes the result to Delorme--Blanc. The paper was received 14 December 1977 and revised 27 October 1978, but these are submission dates, not verified public-release dates. The relative differentiation statement is classical van Est theory, checked in the modern primary treatment \citet[\S3, hypotheses and Theorem 3.3]{wockel2014topological}. That source distinguishes \((\mathfrak g,K)\) from \((\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k)\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established under the explicit assumptions. It is an attributed theorem in the lecture, subsequently documented in Blanc’s 1979 publication; its first public circulation before this meeting is unverified.

title: The unipotent extension of the additive group
notes: The nontrivial extension of the trivial \(\mathbb R\)-module by itself is \(t\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}1&at\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\). A compressed following sentence says there is no correspondence of group and Lie-algebra representations, and mentions triviality on compact subgroups.
statement: For the additive real group and trivial complex coefficients, continuous cocycles are \(f(t)=at\), and coboundaries vanish. Thus \(H^1_{\rm cont}(\mathbb R,\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb C\); the block representation is nonsplit if \(a\ne0\). Its derived nilpotent matrix integrates exactly to this representation of \(\mathbb R\). For the circle instead, every continuous homomorphism to the additive group \(\mathbb C\) vanishes, so \(H^1(S^1,\mathbb C)=0\), whereas its absolute Lie-algebra \(H^1\) is nonzero.
reconstruction: The circle comparison supplies a valid explanation of the compact-subgroup caveat. It is explicitly a reconstruction, since the page writes \(\mathbb R\), whose displayed representation does integrate.
fate: The example follows directly from the cocycle definition and illustrates the role of relative cohomology in van Est comparison \citep[\S3]{wockel2014topological}. No unidentified counterexample to integration over the simply connected additive group is asserted.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The displayed additive-group example is correct; the following compressed sentence cannot literally mean that this representation fails to integrate.

title: The affine group: large ordinary cohomology and zero reduced cohomology
notes: For an irreducible unitary representation of the affine group of the line, the notes assert that \(B^1\) is dense in \(Z^1\), while \(Z^1/B^1\) is infinite-dimensional, and link this to weak containment of the trivial representation.
statement: Use the connected affine group \(G=\mathbb R\rtimes\mathbb R_{>0}\) with \((a,b)(a^{\prime},b^{\prime})=(aa^{\prime},b+ab^{\prime})\), and its irreducible unitary representation on \(L^2(\mathbb R_{>0},dt/t)\), \((\pi(a,b)u)(t)=e^{ibt}u(at)\). Its ordinary continuous \(H^1\) is infinite-dimensional, but the reduced quotient \(Z^1/\overline{B^1}\), using uniform convergence on compact subsets of \(G\), is zero. Nonclosed coboundaries and failure of the ordinary quotient to be Hausdorff are the central distinction; weak containment alone is not a universal proof of infinite-dimensionality for every group.
reconstruction: The specific irreducible representation and topology are supplied. Infinite-dimensionality can be checked using \(u_\alpha(t)=\chi(t)(\log(1/t))^{-\alpha}\), \(0<\alpha\le1/2\), with \(\chi=1\) near zero and supported below \(e^{-1}\): each \(\pi(g)u_\alpha-u_\alpha\) is in \(L^2(dt/t)\), while no nonzero finite linear combination of the \(u_\alpha\) is. These yield independent cocycle classes; an invariant correction cannot occur because the translation action multiplies by \(e^{ibt}\).
fate: Density of coboundaries for this non-character irreducible representation is a direct specialization of \citet[Theorem V.6, page 323]{delorme1977cohomologie}, published in 1977. The elementary family in the reconstruction checks the notebook’s stronger dimensional assertion; the paper’s general density theorem alone is not cited as proving that dimension.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The stated example is established and exhibits why reduced and ordinary first cohomology must be kept distinct.

title: First cohomology of irreducible unitary representations of simple groups
notes: For semisimple groups and irreducible unitary representations, the lecture says it is known when \(H^1\) vanishes, without listing the representations.
statement: For a connected real simple Lie group with finite centre, nontrivial irreducible unitary representations with nonzero continuous first cohomology occur only in the real- and complex-hyperbolic families. For Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{so}(2,1)\) or \(\mathfrak{su}(n,1)\), \(n\ge2\), there are two mutually conjugate complex irreducibles; for \(\mathfrak{so}(n,1)\), \(n\ge3\), there is one. Their \(H^1\) is one-dimensional. Other real simple families have vanishing first cohomology for all unitary representations. Product groups require the corresponding factor analysis rather than a literal transfer of this simple-group count.
reconstruction: The count is an explicit reconstruction of the known result alluded to, restricted to connected simple groups to keep the hypotheses precise. It is not presented as a numerical theorem written in the notebook.
fate: The exceptional counts and dimensions are read in \citet[Theorem V.5, page 317; see also \S V(A) and \S V(C)]{delorme1977cohomologie}. The paper was published in 1977, so this is prior exposition.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The classification cited here is established. The distinction between complex unitary and real orthogonal irreducibles explains why some formulations give one exceptional real representation instead of two conjugate complex ones.

title: Central-character splitting in the smooth category
notes: The second, smooth-vector approach is said to restore the infinitesimal-character lemma, although \(H^1(G,\operatorname{Hom}(E_\infty,F_\infty))\) is difficult to compute.
statement: For an extension in a category of smooth Fréchet representations of a connected Lie group, suppose the derived central operators are continuous and have distinct scalar characters on the end modules. A separating central operator satisfies a polynomial with two distinct roots on the extension. Its polynomial spectral projections are continuous and commute with the group action, and yield a topological equivariant splitting. This argument uses the smooth category and cannot infer boundedness on the original Hilbert or Banach completions.

fate: The natural continuity of derived operators in smooth-vector topology is part of \citet[\S5.1]{blanc1979cohomologie}. present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established for the stated smooth category. No equality with continuous extension groups between arbitrary completions is claimed.

title: K-finite vectors and relative algebraic extensions
notes: The third approach replaces \(E,F\) by \(E_K,F_K\), the vectors lying in finite-dimensional \(K\)-subrepresentations, and writes \(H^1(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k;\operatorname{Hom}(E_K,F_K))\), algebra without topology. title: Semidirect products and dual orbits

title: Quaternionic ADHM reality equations and quotient
notes: For quaternionic \(N\times(N+1)\) matrices \(A,B\), put \(M(x)=xA+B\); require \(MM^+\) real for every quaternion \(x\), modulo \(M\mapsto GMV\), with \(VV^+=1\).
statement: The nondegenerate quaternionic ADHM data for charge \(N\ge1\) consist, in the row-matrix convention, of an affine matrix \(M(x)\) such that \(M(x)M(x)^*\) is real and positive definite for all finite \(x\in\mathbb H\), with the corresponding full-rank condition at infinity. Quotient by \(GL(N,\mathbb R)\) on the left and \(Sp(N+1)\) on the right. Its one-dimensional quaternionic kernel defines an \(SU(2)\) instanton bundle with the orthogonally projected connection; gauge classes of smooth instantons on the round \(S^4\) arise this way, with self-duality sign depending on orientation.
reconstruction: The full-rank condition and the precise groups are supplied from ADHM; quaternion multiplication conventions may be transposed/conjugated when changing row and column conventions. Here \(xA\) means left multiplication of each entry by x. It is compatible with the stated action: \(G(xA+B)V=x(GAV)+GBV\), since G is real and quaternion multiplication is associative. No commutation of x with entries of V is assumed. Passing to the adjoint column convention conjugates x and can reverse the self-duality orientation.
fate: Already announced by \citet[pp.~185--187, reality condition (2) and equivalence paragraph]{atiyahhitchindrinfeldmanin1978instantons}, received 16 December 1977 and published 6 March 1978. The notebook omits the nondegeneracy and the real nature of the left change-of-basis group. Prior-index 1977-451.11 is the same source paragraph under an incorrect year assignment.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The ADHM classification is established. Reality alone also includes degenerate data and must not be equated with the smooth-instanton moduli space.

Prior-index 1977-451.12 is this same paragraph; GP-1977-05 concerns classification and connectedness and must not silently acquire new rationality/global-coordinate quantifiers.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Insufficiently specified for a separate open-problem entry or a bounded research development.

title: Gauge averaging forces a charged bilocal expectation to vanish
notes: Local invariance gives \(\langle\psi(x)\overline\psi(y)\rangle=e^{i(\alpha(x)-\alpha(y))}\langle\psi(x)\overline\psi(y)\rangle\), hence zero.
statement: In a finite-volume lattice gauge theory with compact local gauge group, gauge-invariant measure and action, no gauge fixing, and two distinct sites \(x,y\), an undressed bilocal transforming nontrivially at either site has zero expectation. For an Abelian unit-charge field, averaging an independent phase at \(x\) gives the displayed conclusion. The same argument does not apply to \(x=y\) or to a bilocal completed by a parallel transporter.
reconstruction: The finite lattice, compact gauge group, invariant measure and action, and independent transformations at distinct sites specify a setting in which the averaging argument is valid. These hypotheses are not all stated in the notebook.
fate: This is a gauge-averaging identity of the kind analysed by \citet[Sec.~I]{elitzur1975local}, received 29 July and published 15 December 1975. It is established independently of any confinement phase.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct with gauge-invariant integration and distinct sites; it supplies no confinement criterion.

title: The proposed confinement inference
notes: The vanishing correlation is followed by \ru{невозможность ... для заряж. объектов}; the argument is labelled naive and attributed to Wilson.
statement: The implication ``vanishing of an undressed charged correlator implies physical confinement'' is false without a gauge-invariant confinement observable and a dynamical hypothesis. Gauge averaging also vanishes in a Coulomb regime. A meaningful confinement problem must specify Wilson loops, charge sectors or long-range potentials and the theory and limit involved.
reconstruction: The distinction between a gauge-dependent correlator and a gauge-invariant confinement criterion is an editorial correction; no area-law theorem is reconstructed from the paragraph.
fate: \citet[Introduction and Sec.~IV]{elitzur1975local} explicitly separates local-gauge noninvariant expectation values from physical phase diagnostics. No definite four-dimensional confinement conjecture is formulated on this page; none is inserted here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The inference fails; the incomplete source supplies no exact unsolved problem.

title: A finite cutoff can destroy a hidden symmetry
notes: Passing from a functional integral to a finite multiple integral may break symmetry; the talk is introduced as a discussion of hidden symmetry.
statement: A regulator need not preserve a symmetry of a formal continuum action. To turn this into a theorem one must specify the regulated measure, the transformations and convergence. No regulator or obstruction is identified here.
reconstruction: No choice of ultraviolet regulator or precise hidden symmetry can be recovered. The modern statement only identifies the information needed to turn the sentence into a claim.
fate: \citet[Introduction]{faddeev1996bethe} explains integrability-preserving lattice regularizations in the same programme, but this is only a thematic match to the notebook's general warning; no particular anomaly is asserted.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A methodological observation, not an identifiable open anomaly problem.

title: A semiclassical sine-Gordon spectrum
notes: The equation \(\Box\varphi=\sin\varphi\) is written and the notes say that a quasiclassical spectrum has been obtained.
statement: For the quantized sine-Gordon model in \(1+1\) dimensions, with normal-ordered cosine interaction and a specified coupling/renormalization convention, semiclassical quantization treats solitons and their bound states by fluctuations about classical finite-energy solutions. The page records existence of such a calculation, not a numerical mass formula or an exact remainder estimate.
reconstruction: The distinction between semiclassical asymptotics and an exact spectrum is supplied; no numerical mass formula absent from the notes is attributed to the speaker.
fate: Pre-talk work is surveyed in \citet[abstract and soliton-quantization discussion]{faddeevkorepin1978quantum}, published June 1978; the exact scattering description was already announced by \citet{zamolodchikov1977exact}. These are not later solutions of a problem posed in February 1979.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established semiclassical programme; exact quantum statements require a chosen normalization absent here.

title: The finite periodic XYZ spectral problem
notes: \(H=\sum_{n=1}^N\sum_{a=1}^3J_a\sigma_n^a\sigma_{n+1}^a\), \(\sigma_{N+1}=\sigma_1\), \(J_a\in\mathbb R\); find the eigenvectors and eigenvalues. The notes immediately say Baxter solved it.
statement: For \(N\ge2\), the indicated Hermitian operator acts on \((\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}\). The problem is to diagonalize this finite matrix, including multiplicities and exceptional couplings, using the commuting eight-vertex transfer family. Algebraic diagonalizability is elementary; the substantive issue is an exact integrable description uniform in \(N\).
reconstruction: The finite Hilbert space, multiplicity issue and exceptional-coupling qualification make the spectral question explicit; the notes themselves already call Baxter's problem solved.
fate: Baxter's eight-vertex solution was announced in 1971 \citep{baxter1971eight}, with the eigenvector programme published in the 1973 series \citep{baxter1973eigenvectors}. This is explicitly presented as solved exposition, not a new conjecture. Publication matching for exceptional degeneracies is not claimed from the accessible metadata.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An established exactly solvable family. Singular parametrizations and completeness subtleties must be treated separately from the elementary existence of a spectral decomposition.

title: The chain-to-Thirring scaling limit
notes: Luther reduces the chain to the Thirring model; even and odd sites supply two fermion components, and the continuum theory is related to sine-Gordon.
statement: A continuum low-energy limit of a suitably tuned anisotropic spin chain, after Jordan--Wigner transformation, staggered decomposition, lattice-spacing rescaling and coupling renormalization, yields a massive interacting Dirac theory of Thirring type. This is a scaling limit, not an equality of a fixed finite-dimensional XYZ Hamiltonian with a continuum field operator.
reconstruction: The low-energy regime, tuning, cutoff and renormalization qualifications are supplied from the identified scaling-limit interpretation. No specified topology of convergence is claimed.
fate: \citet[abstract, pp.~2153--2159]{luther1976eigenvalue} computes the excitation spectrum and identifies the corresponding massive Thirring/sine-Gordon couplings; received 19 April and published 1 September 1976.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established correspondence in the stated scaling regime; the notebook omits the scaling prescription and cannot support convergence in a specified operator topology.

title: Pauli spin algebra
notes: The three standard Pauli matrices are displayed, but (2) writes \([\sigma_n^a,\sigma_n^b]=\varepsilon_{abc}\sigma_n^c\).
statement: With exactly the displayed matrices, \([\sigma_n^a,\sigma_m^b]=2i\delta_{nm}\sum_c\varepsilon_{abc}\sigma_n^c\) and \(\{\sigma_n^a,\sigma_n^b\}=2\delta_{ab}I\). Tensor factors at distinct sites commute.
reconstruction: The corrected factor and different-site commutator are obtained directly from the matrices printed in the notes.
fate: This is the standard local spin algebra used in \citet[Sec.~3]{faddeev1996bethe}; the factor \(2i\) is also checked directly from the displayed \(2\times2\) matrices. The scan faithfully lacks it.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected identities are exact; the error is mathematical shorthand in the notebook, not an English translation error.

title: Jordan--Wigner fermions and their normalization
notes: \(\psi_n^\pm=(\sigma_n^1\pm i\sigma_n^2)\prod_{m<n}\sigma_m^3\) is claimed to satisfy \(\{\psi_n^-,\psi_m^+\}=\delta_{nm}\).
statement: For a finite ordered spin chain, define \(c_n=\frac12(\sigma_n^1-i\sigma_n^2)\prod_{m<n}\sigma_m^3\). Then \(\{c_n,c_m\}=0\), \(\{c_n,c_m^\dagger\}=\delta_{nm}I\). Without the factor \(1/2\), the latter right side is \(4\delta_{nm}I\). A periodic spin chain produces a fermion-parity-dependent boundary term.
reconstruction: The factor one-half and periodic-boundary parity qualification are supplied; the normalization is checked directly from the printed matrices.
fate: The construction and fermionic solution of chain models are pre-talk material \citep{liebschultzmattis1961soluble}. The normalization follows directly from the displayed Pauli matrices; the missing periodic parity condition is essential for a finite-chain spectrum.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The canonical anticommutation relations hold exactly after correction, with parity sectors retained at periodic boundaries.

title: Quadratic fermion diagonalization of the transverse Ising chain
notes: Expressing spins through fermions makes the Hamiltonian quadratic; the concrete example is \(H=\sum_n(\sigma_n^1\sigma_{n+1}^1+\Delta\sigma_n^3)\). A Fourier transform is proposed.
statement: For the transverse Ising chain the Jordan--Wigner image is quadratic in creation and annihilation operators, and a Fourier--Bogoliubov transformation diagonalizes each fixed parity sector. For a general XYZ chain the \(J_3\sigma_n^3\sigma_{n+1}^3\) term yields quartic density interactions, so the quadratic assertion is restricted to the Ising/free-fermion example.
reconstruction: Quadratic fermions, the absence of a longitudinal interaction and the treatment of the boundary parity sector specify the solvable specialization.
fate: This is part of the pre-1979 free-fermion method \citep{liebschultzmattis1961soluble}. Onsager's 1944 solution uses a related transfer/Clifford structure \citep[Secs.~II--VII]{onsager1944crystal}; the notebook compresses these related implementations into one historical sentence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Exact in the specified free-fermion model, not for arbitrary XYZ couplings.

title: Heisenberg evolution preserves the algebra, but the displayed equation is schematic
notes: Equation (7) is \(\dot\sigma=i[\sigma,H]\); after fermionization (8) becomes \(\dot\psi_n=\psi_{n+1}-\psi_{n-1}\).
statement: Unitary conjugation preserves every polynomial operator relation. With the usual convention \(U(t)=e^{-itH}\), Heisenberg evolution satisfies \(\dot O=i[H,O]\). For the transverse Ising chain, the fermion equations are linear in both \(c\) and \(c^\dagger\), and depend on \(\Delta\); the printed single-component, \(\Delta\)-independent equation is not its general equation of motion.
reconstruction: The time-evolution convention is stated explicitly. Dependence on the transverse field and coupling to adjoint fermions are corrections to the schematic displayed equation.
fate: The quadratic solution framework is already in \citet{liebschultzmattis1961soluble}. The missing \(\Delta\) term and adjoint coupling follow by direct commutation with (6), so no later theorem repairs (8) as a literal statement.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Algebra preservation is exact. Equation (8) requires a different specialization or variables not supplied by the notes.

title: Interacting fermions and the continuum quartic term
notes: The original chain gives a schematic quartic Hamiltonian (9), followed by a continuum expression with \(\psi_1^+\psi_2\psi_1^+\psi_2^+\).
statement: A nonzero longitudinal XYZ coupling produces a density-density term \(n_n n_{n+1}\), in addition to quadratic hopping and, for transverse anisotropy, pairing. A continuum Thirring interaction is a regularized current-current product \(\frac g2 j_\mu j^\mu\), \(j^\mu=\overline\psi\gamma^\mu\psi\). The printed repeated \(\psi_1^+\) expression does not specify that product and cannot be repaired uniquely without conventions and point splitting.
reconstruction: The regularized current-current expression is the identified continuum interaction, not a unique emendation of the malformed monomial in the notebook.
fate: The lattice/continuum identification predates the talk \citep{luther1976eigenvalue,coleman1975equivalence}. The quartic monomial is retained as a faithful source error or unresolved shorthand, rather than silently replaced with a guessed sequence of indices.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The current-current interaction is established; the exact literal continuum expression is not a usable Hamiltonian.

title: Massive Thirring and quantum sine-Gordon equivalence
notes: The notes attribute the 1975 equivalence to Mandelstam and an omitted name.
statement: In Coleman's normal-ordering convention, the massive Thirring and sine-Gordon theories have matching neutral-sector correlation functions with \(4\pi/\beta^2=1+g/\pi\), after matching the mass parameters and operator normalization. The equivalence is a quantum field-theoretic statement with regularization; it is not established by equating their unregularized classical equations.
reconstruction: The neutral sector, normal ordering, operator normalization and coupling convention are supplied from Coleman's formulation.
fate: The omitted name is Sidney Coleman: \citet[abstract, pp.~2088--2097]{coleman1975equivalence}, received 6 January and published 15 April 1975; \citet{mandelstam1975soliton}, received 24 February and published 15 May 1975, constructs the soliton fields.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A standard equivalence with explicitly specified operator and coupling conventions; no open problem was posed here.

title: Mandelstam soliton operators and canonical factors
notes: Equations (12)--(14) write \([\dot\varphi(x),\varphi(y)]=\delta(x-y)\), an unnormal-ordered exponential, and \(\alpha\beta=4\pi\).
statement: For a canonically normalized real boson, \([\varphi(t,x),\Pi(t,y)]=i\delta(x-y)\), hence \([\Pi,\varphi]=-i\delta\). Fermion fields can be represented by regulated normal-ordered vertex/disorder operators of the schematic form \(C:\!\exp[-i(\frac{2\pi}{\beta}\int_{-\infty}^x\Pi\,dy\pm\frac\beta2\varphi(x))]\!:\), with component/Klein factors and cutoff normalization. Their exchange signs and delta-function normalization depend on this full prescription.
reconstruction: This regulated vertex operator is a schematic reconstruction. The notebook does not supply its component signs, cutoff or Klein factors. No unique repair of its alpha-beta relation is asserted.
fate: \citet[abstract and operator construction]{mandelstam1975soliton} explicitly constructs operators satisfying the Thirring equations and anticommutation relations. The scan confirms the missing imaginary factors and gives no normal-ordering prescription; its \(\alpha\beta=4\pi\) cannot be accepted with the unqualified displayed conventions.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established regulated bosonization; the raw notebook exponential and CCR are not literal quantum-operator identities.

title: The Zamolodchikov exchange algebra
notes: Generators \(A_i(\theta)\) exchange through \(S(\theta_1-\theta_2)\); the printed range \(1\le i<M\) is inconsistent with the following \(M=2\) example using \(A_2\).
statement: For \(V=\mathbb C^M\), use indices \(1\le i\le M\). Introduce generators \(A_i(\theta)\) with quadratic exchange rules determined by a meromorphic two-body matrix \(S(u)\in\operatorname{End}(V\otimes V)\), where the output generators have interchanged rapidities. This defines an associative quotient algebra; requiring noncollapsed, consistently ordered scattering states imposes further conditions on \(S\).
reconstruction: The inclusive index range, fixed permutation convention and distinction between an associative quotient and independent ordered states are editorial clarifications.
fate: The factorized scattering framework predates the talk \citep[Secs.~1--3]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on}; the sine-Gordon two-particle solution appeared in 1977 \citep{zamolodchikov1977exact}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established algebraic framework after the index-range correction and the distinction between quotient associativity and nondegenerate exchange consistency.

title: Three-particle consistency and factorization
notes: Associativity of a three-generator product is said to impose the condition on \(S\) that leads to factorized multiparticle scattering.
statement: If three-particle ordered states with distinct rapidities are linearly independent and pair exchanges act by invertible two-body matrices, consistency of the two reorderings gives \(R_{12}(u)R_{13}(u+v)R_{23}(v)=R_{23}(v)R_{13}(u+v)R_{12}(u)\), with \(R\) defined according to a fixed permutation convention. The Yang--Baxter equation alone does not establish absence of particle production in a given QFT.
reconstruction: Invertibility, linear independence and absence of particle production are additional hypotheses; associativity of an arbitrary quotient alone is insufficient.
fate: The consistency equations are explicit in \citet[Sec.~2]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on}; a later precise matrix presentation is \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{belavin1980discrete}. These sources distinguish the algebraic constraint from the physical identification of a model.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established under the stated factorized-scattering hypotheses; merely forming an associative quotient does not force a Yang--Baxter matrix.

title: Baxter elliptic weights and their limited completeness claim
notes: The four weights are \(a=\operatorname{sn}(\theta+\eta,k)\), \(b=\operatorname{sn}(\theta-\eta,k)\), \(c=\operatorname{sn}(2\eta,k)\), \(d=kabc\); these are said to be all solutions up to a factor.
statement: In the zero-field eight-vertex ansatz \(R(u)=\begin{psmallmatrix}a&0&0&d\\0&b&c&0\\0&c&b&0\\d&0&0&a\end{psmallmatrix}\), a standard regular parametrization is \(a=\operatorname{sn}(u+\eta_0,k)\), \(b=\operatorname{sn}(u,k)\), \(c=\operatorname{sn}(\eta_0,k)\), \(d=kabc\), divided by \(c\ne0\). Then \(R(0)=P\). The notebook form is obtained with \(u=\theta-\eta\), \(\eta_0=2\eta\); that spectral-origin change must also be respected in the addition law. No unrestricted classification of all \(4\times4\) Yang--Baxter solutions follows.
reconstruction: The regular spectral origin and nonzero normalizing denominator are supplied explicitly. The restricted eight-vertex ansatz does not support the literal unrestricted completeness claim.
fate: The eight-vertex solution is pre-talk Baxter material \citep{baxter1971eight}. Belavin later constructed higher-dimensional solutions with additional discrete symmetry \citep[pp.~189--200]{belavin1981dynamical}; this is not evidence for the notebook's unrestricted ``all solutions'' sentence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The elliptic eight-vertex family is established; origin, degenerations, gauge transformations and imposed symmetries delimit any completeness assertion.

title: Transfer matrices and commuting Hamiltonians
notes: The cyclic contraction of \(N\) copies of \(S\) defines \(T(\theta)\), a \(2^N\times2^N\) matrix, and satisfies \([T(\theta),H]=[T(\theta_1),T(\theta_2)]=0\).
statement: For a meromorphic, generically invertible difference-form \(R\) satisfying Yang--Baxter, define \(t(u)=\operatorname{tr}_a R_{aN}(u)\cdots R_{a1}(u)\). Then \([t(u),t(v)]=0\). If \(R(0)=P\), the logarithmic derivative \(t(0)^{-1}t'(0)\) is a periodic nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian, up to scalar normalization/additive constants, and commutes with every \(t(u)\). At fixed \(N\), an infinite Taylor list need not be algebraically independent.
reconstruction: Generic invertibility, regularity, the auxiliary trace and the restriction on independence at fixed chain length are supplied to make the standard construction precise.
fate: The pre-talk transfer construction is recalled explicitly by \citet[eqs.~(3)--(6)]{belavin1980discrete}; the complete RTT/trace derivation and Hamiltonian derivative are given by \citet[Sec.~3, eqs.~(44)--(65)]{faddeev1996bethe}, based on his 1995 lectures, first posted May 1996.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established finite-dimensional identities. The phrase ``infinite set of integrals'' describes a generating series or varying-chain hierarchy, not infinitely many independent operators on a fixed finite chain.

title: Exchange generators and associativity
notes: The \ru{Алгебра Замолодчикова} has generators \(A_i(\theta)\), \(1\le i\le M\), quadratic exchange rules and a requirement of associativity.
statement: For \(V=\mathbb C^M\), an exchange matrix \(S(u)\) specifies relations between generators with interchanged spectral parameters. Their quotient of the tensor algebra is associative by construction. A nondegenerate ordered-state interpretation requires that the exchange relations do not introduce inconsistent additional dependencies.
reconstruction: The tensor-algebra and nondegeneracy distinction clarifies the notebook's shorthand.
fate: The construction is pre-talk factorized-scattering material \citep[Sec.~2]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on}. The distinction between quotient associativity and a basis of ordered states is essential to the next assertion.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A standard construction; associativity alone is not a test for a Yang--Baxter matrix.

title: Rapidity ordering and collision diagrams
notes: The parameters \(\theta_i\) are called velocities; two collision histories are identified because only the initial and final order matters.
statement: For massive relativistic particles in \(1+1\) dimensions, rapidity satisfies \(E=m\cosh\theta\), \(p=m\sinh\theta\), \(v=\tanh\theta\). A difference-form two-body amplitude depends on rapidity differences. Equating the two three-particle collision orderings presupposes elastic factorized scattering with well-defined asymptotic states.
reconstruction: Rapidity replaces literal velocity; the scattering assumptions are made explicit.
fate: These are the physical hypotheses of \citet[Secs.~1--2]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on}, published February 1978. Its authors expressly distinguish a consistent proposed S-matrix from identification with a particular field theory.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established kinematics and conditional factorization argument, not a proof that every two-dimensional theory factorizes.

title: Three-body reordering and the Yang--Baxter equation
notes: Two reorderings of \(A_i(\theta_1)A_j(\theta_2)A_k(\theta_3)\) lead to equation (2); the last generator on P000816 is written \(A_i(\theta)\).
statement: For linearly independent ordered three-particle states and a fixed unbraided convention, consistency is \(R_{12}(u)R_{13}(u+v)R_{23}(v)=R_{23}(v)R_{13}(u+v)R_{12}(u)\). The last factor in the displayed reordering must carry the final contracted index and original rapidity, \(A_{i_2}(\theta_1)\).
reconstruction: The leg convention, independence and repaired dummy indices are supplied; the notebook's component indices are not silently treated as reliable.
fate: The matrix relation is already present in the factorized-scattering programme \citep[Sec.~2]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on}; \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{belavin1980discrete} gives an explicit later matrix formulation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected Yang--Baxter identity is standard; a relation in a collapsed quotient would not imply it.

title: The component count of the consistency equations
notes: There are \(M^6\) equations for \(M^4\) functions \(S_{ik}^{\alpha\beta}(\theta)\).
statement: An endomorphism of \(V^{\otimes3}\) has \(M^6\) matrix entries, whereas one of \(V^{\otimes2}\) has \(M^4\). Thus the Yang--Baxter identity supplies this many displayed component equations for this many scalar matrix functions. This is a raw count, with no claim that the equations are independent.
reconstruction: The distinction between a raw component count and independent constraints is supplied.
fate: The count follows directly from the matrix formulation \citep[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{belavin1980discrete}; symmetries and identities can substantially reduce the system.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An exact dimension count with no classification consequence by itself.

title: Cyclic contraction and commuting transfer matrices
notes: Equation (3) cyclically contracts \(N\) copies of \(S\) into an \(M^N\times M^N\) matrix; (4) asserts pairwise commutation.
statement: For a generically invertible meromorphic Yang--Baxter matrix on \(V\otimes V\), the periodic transfer matrix \(t(u)=\operatorname{tr}_aR_{aN}(u)\cdots R_{a1}(u)\) satisfies \([t(u),t(v)]=0\). Invertibility is used in the auxiliary-space intertwining argument; the identity then continues meromorphically.
reconstruction: The auxiliary trace, analytic domain and invertibility hypothesis supply the proof's missing structure.
fate: This is pre-talk transfer-matrix theory. A complete RTT and trace proof appears in \citet[Sec.~3, eqs.~(44)--(65)]{faddeev1996bethe}, lectures of 1995 posted in May 1996; Belavin recalls it in \citet[eqs.~(3)--(6)]{belavin1980discrete}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established, including inhomogeneous variants not needed for the literal notes.

title: Conservation laws as a route to factorization
notes: \ru{Факториз. \(S\)-матр. --- следствие кон. числа законов сохр.}
statement: In a massive relativistic scattering theory, suitable nontrivial higher-spin local conserved charges, acting additively and with nondegenerate momentum dependence on asymptotic particles, can constrain scattering to elastic factorized processes. Merely having a finite number of conserved quantities, for example energy and momentum alone, is not sufficient.
reconstruction: Higher-spin, locality, additivity and nondegeneracy are necessary qualifications to the identified argument; the exact minimal list of charges is not recoverable here.
fate: \citet[Sec.~1]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on} states the physical higher-conservation-law setting. The notebook's unrestricted finite-number assertion has no matched theorem with its literal quantifiers.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The conditional mechanism is established. The bare finite-number assertion is false.

title: The four-weight eight-vertex ansatz
notes: For \(M=2\), four functions \(a,b,c,d\) are retained from sixteen possible entries; the note mentions five or six more general functions and parenthetically Maxwell's equations.
statement: The zero-field eight-vertex ansatz is \(R=\begin{pmatrix}a&0&0&d\\0&b&c&0\\0&c&b&0\\d&0&0&a\end{pmatrix}\). Homogeneity of Yang--Baxter permits division by a nonzero scalar function, so \(c=1\) is a local normalization wherever \(c\ne0\). Neither a five-or-six-function classification nor a Maxwell equation identification is specified.
reconstruction: The symmetry-restricted matrix and the domain of scalar normalization are made explicit. The Maxwell parenthesis is retained without interpretation.
fate: The restricted ansatz is Baxter's pre-talk construction \citep{baxter1971eight}. The unelaborated parenthesis and numerical generality claim have no exact publication match in the sources checked.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established eight-vertex specialization; the omitted general ansatz cannot be reconstructed uniquely.

title: An inconsistent sample functional equation
notes: Equation (6), after setting \(c=1\), is \(a(u)a(u+v)d(v)=d(u+v)a(v)+b(u)b(u+v)d(v)\). Equation (7) requires \(R(0)=P\).
statement: In the displayed four-weight convention regularity means \(a(0)=c(0)=1\), \(b(0)=d(0)=0\). Substituting \(v=0\) in the printed (6) yields \(0=d(u)\). Thus the printed equation cannot describe a regular elliptic eight-vertex family with nonzero \(d\).
reconstruction: The contradiction is an elementary substitution using the notebook's own initial condition; only the diagnosis, not a unique intended equation, is reconstructed.
fate: Baxter's elliptic family exists \citep{baxter1971eight}; the conflict is internal to the notebook. The precise missing factor or argument in (6) has not been uniquely recovered, so no guessed correction replaces it.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Literal inconsistency established. The exact intended component equation remains unidentified.

title: Differential reduction and elliptic solutions
notes: Differentiating the functional system is said to yield four displayed ODEs and two omitted ones, with \(a'(0)=\alpha\), \(b'(0)=\beta\), \(d'(0)=\gamma\). Two independent algebraic constraints then lead to elliptic functions.
statement: For a differentiable regular Yang--Baxter solution, differentiating the full functional equations at one parameter zero gives necessary ODEs, with first derivatives encoding local couplings. Integrating an incomplete ODE list is not sufficient for the original functional equation. The notebook's (6) already fails the regularity test, and the two unprinted ODEs and algebraic constraints cannot be recovered solely from this page.
reconstruction: The necessary-versus-sufficient distinction and requirement to check the full functional equation are supplied. No omitted equation is invented.
fate: The elliptic eight-vertex result is known before the talk \citep{baxter1971eight}; the precise displayed differential system is only a partial, faulty transcription of that method. It is not used here to assert a new classification.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The differential method is standard; the notebook's incomplete system does not identify an independently verifiable theorem.

title: Representing an unspecified algebra of four functions
notes: A noncommutative, nonassociative algebra of quadruples is said to arise. Find an explicit realization, for example by matrices. Manin suggests torsion points of an elliptic curve.
statement: The page specifies neither a multiplication of quadruples nor the relations to be represented. Ordinary matrix multiplication is associative, so a faithful realization of a genuinely nonassociative algebra would require a different operation. Torsion points alone do not define such an operation.
reconstruction: Only the missing structural data are identified. No later Sklyanin or elliptic algebra is substituted for the unspecified object.
fate: Belavin's later elliptic constructions use discrete groups \citep[eqs.~(7)--(17)]{belavin1980discrete}; his 1981 paper concerns dynamical symmetry \citep{belavin1981dynamical}. These are thematic leads, not an exact identification of this missing algebra.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: No definite representability problem can be extracted. It is not classified as an unresolved modern conjecture.

title: Commuting Taylor coefficients
notes: From \(T(u)=\sum_{\ell\ge0}I_\ell u^\ell\) the notes infer \([I_n,I_m]=0\).
statement: If a matrix-valued function \(T\) is analytic near zero and \([T(u),T(v)]=0\) for independent \(u,v\), coefficient comparison gives \([I_n,I_m]=0\) for all \(n,m\). The same holds formally for a commuting formal power series.
reconstruction: Analyticity or formal-series interpretation is supplied.
fate: This is a direct consequence of the established transfer-matrix relation \citep[Sec.~3]{faddeev1996bethe}, with no later mathematical problem attached.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Exact coefficient identity; infinitely many coefficients need not be independent for fixed finite N.

title: The XYZ Hamiltonian as a logarithmic derivative
notes: Equation (11) gives \(I_0^{-1}I_1=T(0)^{-1}T'(0)=\sum_{n,a}J_a\sigma_n^a\sigma_{n+1}^a\), and all \(I_\ell\) commute with it.
statement: For an analytic regular eight-vertex matrix with \(R(0)=P\), the transfer matrix at zero is the cyclic shift, hence invertible. Its first logarithmic derivative is a sum of translated copies of \(h=PR'(0)\), which has XYZ form up to a scalar identity and convention-dependent coupling normalization.
reconstruction: Regularity, the shift and the scalar normalization are supplied.
fate: This pre-talk construction is recorded in \citet[eqs.~(3)--(6)]{belavin1980discrete}; the regular-point derivation is spelled out in \citet[Sec.~3]{faddeev1996bethe}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established local Hamiltonian construction from the regular transfer family.

title: Local three-site charges versus raw Taylor coefficients
notes: The notes say that \(I_2\) contains three spins, and similarly for higher coefficients.
statement: Local higher charges are obtained from derivatives of \(\log(t(u)t(0)^{-1})\), with conventions for their index and factorial. The second such derivative is \(t(0)^{-1}t''(0)-[t(0)^{-1}t'(0)]^2\). The subtraction cancels disconnected products; a raw Taylor coefficient \(I_2\) generally contains nonlocal products as well.
reconstruction: The logarithmic generating function is the required correction; it is not written in the notebook for the higher coefficients.
fate: This is the local-charge organization of the transfer hierarchy \citep[Sec.~3]{faddeev1996bethe}. The notebook's raw-coefficient locality assertion is not literally correct.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The local hierarchy is established; raw Taylor coefficients must not be described as single three-site densities.

title: Gelfand suggests SL(2,R)
notes: \ru{И. М. Г. \quad a,b,c,d --- наверное, \(SL(2,R)\)}.
statement: Four scalar functions do not specify an element, representation or coordinate system of \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) without a determinant relation, real form and multiplication law. None is stated.
reconstruction: No group identification is reconstructed from the tentative wording.
fate: The nearby eight-vertex and elliptic-symmetry literature \citep{baxter1971eight,belavin1981dynamical} supplies context but not a proposition equivalent to this tentative remark.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An unformulated analogy, not a surviving precise research problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The six-vertex trigonometric degeneration
notes: Setting \(d=0\) gives ordinary trigonometric rather than elliptic functions.
statement: Within Baxter's family, sending the elliptic modulus to zero gives \(\operatorname{sn}(u,0)=\sin u\) and \(d=0\), hence the six-vertex/XXZ trigonometric family, with a rational limit after further scaling. Merely imposing \(d=0\) does not classify all degenerate solutions.
reconstruction: The modulus limit, domain and rational degeneration delimit the intended claim.
fate: This is a degeneration of the pre-talk eight-vertex solution \citep{baxter1971eight}; the trigonometric higher-spin framework is explicitly developed in \citet{bytsko2003xxz}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established restricted degeneration, without an unrestricted completeness assertion.

title: Arbitrary auxiliary dimension and a nearest-neighbour density
notes: Equations (13) and (17) replace Pauli matrices by matrix units and form \(H=I_0^{-1}I_1\) for general \(M\).
statement: For \(V=\mathbb C^M\) and analytic regular Yang--Baxter \(R\), the periodic Hamiltonian is \(H=\sum_n h_{n,n+1}\), \(h=PR'(0)\), with the contraction order fixed by the chosen convention. Matrix units \(E_{ij}\) span every two-site operator. The spanning statement does not imply that every two-site operator is the derivative of a Yang--Baxter family.
reconstruction: Analyticity, regularity and the distinction between arbitrary density and integrable density are supplied.
fate: The regular transfer-matrix derivative is standard \citep[Sec.~3]{faddeev1996bethe}; its converse has nontrivial obstructions, exemplified by the audited spin-one density.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established forward construction. Its unrestricted converse is false.

title: The literal rotationally invariant spin-1 density
notes: The displayed density is \(h=X^2-2X\), \(X=\sum_aS^a\otimes S^a\), while the next page fixes \([S^a,S^b]=\varepsilon_{abc}S^c\) in the real standard/adjoint representation of \(SO(3)\). It is attributed to a Zamolodchikov solution.
statement: With exactly that normalization, \(X=K-P\), where \(P\) flips the factors and \(K(e_i\otimes e_j)=\delta_{ij}\sum_a e_a\otimes e_a\). For \(h_t=X^2+tX\), the matrix entry \(\langle001|[h_{12}+h_{23},[h_{12},h_{23}]]|212\rangle=t(t-1)(t+1)\). It is \(-6\) at the printed \(t=-2\), whereas every \(Q_{23}-Q_{12}\) has zero in that entry. Therefore this density, even up to nonzero scale and added identity, cannot arise from an analytic regular difference-form braided R-matrix.
reconstruction: The analytic regular difference-form scope is explicitly supplied. The exact obstruction is this chapter's critical algebraic audit, not a claim about every possible notion of integrability. In Hermitian generators \(J^a=iS^a\), the familiar isotropic density is proportional to \(J\cdot J-(J\cdot J)^2\), not to the notebook expression.
fate: The necessary condition is reviewed by \citet[Sec.~2, eqs.~(1)--(6)]{zhang2025bootstrap}, first posted April 2025, checked version February 2026. The chapter derives it and computes the obstruction independently twice. The intended published density is not identifiable from the printed coefficient; the known spin-one model has a different bilinear/biquadratic ratio \citep[Sec.~5]{bytsko2003xxz}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The literal regular difference-form claim is excluded by an exact necessary-condition calculation. The historical intended coefficient remains uncertain.

title: Uniqueness of an invariant two-site spin-one-half interaction
notes: For \(M=2\), \(H=\sum_n\vec\sigma_n\cdot\vec\sigma_{n+1}\); the notes say there is nothing else invariant for spin one-half.
statement: On \(\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2\), the diagonal \(SU(2)\) representation splits as one spin-zero and one spin-one summand. Its commutant is two-dimensional, spanned by \(I\) and \(P\), equivalently \(I\) and \(\sum_a\sigma^a\otimes\sigma^a\). Thus a rotationally invariant two-site density has one nontrivial coupling after adding constants and scaling. This does not classify interactions involving more sites.
reconstruction: Two-site support and the quotient by additive constants are the omitted scope restrictions.
fate: This elementary representation-theoretic fact underlies the Heisenberg example \citep[Sec.~3]{faddeev1996bethe}; the signs of ferromagnetic versus antiferromagnetic couplings require an energy convention.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Exact elementary classification in the stated two-site setting.

title: Adding anisotropic parameters to the spin-1 construction
notes: \ru{Неизвестно, как к гам. (14) добавить параметры, чтобы уложиться в сх. Замолодчикова.}
statement: The literal question asks for a family of regular factorizing matrices whose local Hamiltonian reduces to (14). Under the analytic difference-form interpretation used in the transfer construction, no such family can pass through the printed density, by item 1978-454.17. A separate corrected question asks for anisotropic integrable deformations of the isotropic spin-one density \(J\cdot J-(J\cdot J)^2\).
reconstruction: The regular analytic difference-form scope comes from the preceding construction. The correctly normalized isotropic reference Hamiltonian is an explicitly separate reconstruction, not an emendation asserted to be the speaker's intention.
fate: The nearby corrected problem was answered by \citet[pp.~298--303]{zamolodchikovfateev1980spin}, published in 1980; an earlier circulation date was not verified. \citet[Sec.~5, eqs.~(52)--(55)]{bytsko2003xxz}, preprint December 2001, explicitly identifies the resulting spin-one XXZ Hamiltonian and its isotropic limit. That is a partial match because the literal coefficient in (14) differs.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The literal regular-family extension is excluded; the corrected spin-one anisotropic construction is established. No unresolved remainder is manufactured from the coefficient error.

title: The proposed universality of the factorization scheme
notes: The scheme is said to contain all completely integrable two-dimensional quantum systems, and classical systems after a semiclassical limit.
statement: No definition of complete integrability, class of field theories, scattering assumptions, limiting parameter or convergence of a classical limit is given. Consequently an all-systems classification theorem cannot be extracted. A regular finite-dimensional difference R-matrix construction is a precise sufficient framework, not this unspecified universal quantifier.
reconstruction: The statement records exactly which quantifiers and definitions are absent; no universal theorem is substituted.
fate: The checked original factorized-scattering paper \citep[Secs.~1--3]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on} treats particular massive models and identification issues, not the asserted universal classification.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Too broad to identify as a definite theorem or open problem.

title: Gelfand asks for a Maurer-Cartan interpretation
notes: \ru{Вопрос И.М.Г.: соотн. на S --- типа Маурера--Картана}.
statement: A precise Maurer--Cartan interpretation requires a specified differential graded or higher algebra, a degree-one object representing S and an equation equivalent to the given Yang--Baxter relation. The notebook supplies none of these.
reconstruction: No differential, graded bracket or deformation complex is reconstructed.
fate: Later algebraic interpretations of Yang--Baxter equations are a broad thematic continuation. The checked Belavin constructions \citep{belavin1980discrete,belavin1981dynamical} do not identify an exact theorem with this unformulated question.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A suggestive but unquantified analogy; not eligible for an open-problem or development claim.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Second-order extension does not make every local Hamiltonian integrable
notes: The most general nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian is said always to have a nontrivial integral because \(S''(0)\) can be reconstructed from \(S'(0)\).
statement: Even when a regular Yang--Baxter expansion can be normalized so that \(\check R''(0)=h^2\), its cubic coefficient requires \([h_{12}+h_{23},[h_{12},h_{23}]]=Q_{23}-Q_{12}\). Arbitrary densities do not satisfy this condition. A second-order formal jet alone gives neither a full R-matrix nor a nontrivial independent local conserved charge.
reconstruction: A precise regular expansion and cubic obstruction replace the unsupported inference. The undefined word nontrivial is not interpreted as a new general integrability theorem.
fate: The obstruction is the standard necessary Reshetikhin condition \citep[Sec.~2]{zhang2025bootstrap}. The exact spin-one calculation in this chapter supplies an explicit failure of the notebook's proposed automatic extension.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: False as an unrestricted assertion; a finite Taylor jet is insufficient.

title: Matrix associativity is not enough for exchange consistency
notes: If the \(A_i(\theta)\) are matrices, associativity is automatic.
statement: Matrix multiplication is associative. However, a finite-dimensional representation of exchange relations can have dependent or vanishing products, so associativity of that representation alone does not imply an equality of abstract coefficient tensors such as Yang--Baxter.
reconstruction: The failure of coefficient comparison without independence is supplied.
fate: This clarifies the ordered-state hypothesis in the original construction \citep[Sec.~2]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on}. It is an elementary logical distinction, not a missing later solution.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The literal associativity observation is true, but its suggested sufficiency for solving the coefficient equations is not.

title: Monodromy multiplication and RTT representations
notes: An untraced product of local S-matrices gives matrix-valued blocks \(L^{ik}\); equation (20) asserts the same exchange relation for L. Equation (21) calls these blocks a new higher-order algebra.
statement:
If each local L-operator satisfies
\[R_{ab}(u-v)L_{an}(u)L_{bn}(v)=L_{bn}(v)L_{an}(u)R_{ab}(u-v),\]
and distinct quantum sites commute, their ordered product satisfies the same RTT relation. Its entries act on \(V^{\otimes N}\). Thus tensor products of local representations generate larger representations; the blocks need not literally obey the one-index Zamolodchikov algebra without an additional identification.
reconstruction: Independent quantum sites and the RTT rather than one-index exchange convention are supplied. The broken internal chain of indices in (18) is repaired by the unambiguous ordered-product definition.
fate: The multiplication identity is an algebraic consequence of the pre-talk Yang--Baxter method. The quantum inverse-scattering programme was announced by \citet[Secs.~1--3]{sklyaninfaddeev1978quantum}, submitted July and published December 1978; that short paper is not claimed to contain every later RTT formulation. A complete multiplication and trace derivation is read in \citet[Sec.~3, eqs.~(44)--(65)]{faddeev1996bethe}. Prior-index 1977-436.16 is a thematic link to the quantum inverse-scattering programme, not the same finite spectral or spin-one deformation question.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established representation multiplication; the literal index string contains a faithful source error.

title: The zero-field Ising partition sum and trace
notes: For periodic spins \(\sigma_{n,m}=\pm1\), (22) sums horizontal and vertical nearest-neighbour weights; (23) writes \(Z=\operatorname{Tr}T^N\).
statement: For an \(N\times M\) torus with dimensionless couplings \(K_1,K_2\) and zero magnetic field, let \(T_{s,t}=\exp\{\frac{K_1}{2}\sum_j(s_js_{j+1}+t_jt_{j+1})+K_2\sum_js_jt_j\}\), with periodic j. Then expanding the trace gives the stated finite partition sum exactly: \(Z=\operatorname{Tr}T^N\).
reconstruction: The explicit symmetric row-transfer convention and lattice dimensions are supplied as one realization of the trace identity; the notebook later sketches a diagonal transfer instead.
fate: The transfer method and anisotropic zero-field solution are already in \citet[Secs.~II--VII]{onsager1944crystal}, received October 1943 and published 1944. The notebook's separate unexplained 1965 attribution of commuting transfer matrices is not used as an established priority claim.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Exact finite combinatorial identity, and an established zero-field solvable model.

title: Diagonal transfer weights and an unfinished commutation assertion
notes: The diagonal drawing sums spins on intermediate diagonals, writes \(T_{\vec\alpha\vec\beta}=S_1\cdots S_n\), and ends \ru{\(T(J_1,J_2)\) коммут. пр}, apparently the beginning of a conditional assertion.
statement: Diagonal transfer matrices can be assembled by contracting local Boltzmann weights, with torus dimensions and boundary identifications specified. Commutation of two transfer matrices is an additional relation between their couplings or spectral parameters. The page does not state that relation, so no literal two-parameter commutation theorem is recoverable.
reconstruction: The local contraction is identifiable; the missing commutation condition is deliberately not supplied as though present in the notes.
fate: Onsager's transfer-operator analysis \citep{onsager1944crystal} and Baxter's subsequent commuting families \citep{baxter1971eight} provide context. They do not identify the missing words or determine which transfer convention the final assertion used.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Incomplete source statement. No open question is inferred from a line that simply stops.

title: The Grassmannian compactification of complex Minkowski space
notes: \(\widehat{\mathbb CM}=G(4,2)\), the two-planes in \(\mathbb C^4\), contains an open subset isomorphic to \(\mathbb C^4\).
statement: Put \(X=\operatorname{Gr}(2,\mathbb C^4)\). For a splitting \(\mathbb C^4=U\oplus W\), planes transverse to W are graphs of \(Z\in\operatorname{Hom}(U,W)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\). Their tangent space carries the conformal quadratic form \(q(dZ)=\det(dZ)\), well-defined up to scale under changes of chart. Thus X is compactified complex conformal four-space, with affine Minkowski charts.
reconstruction: The graph chart and determinant conformal structure spell out the compactification; they are not fully written on the page.
fate: This is classical twistor geometry before 1979, reviewed by \citet[Secs.~1--2]{penrosemaccallum1973twistor}; the graph coordinates and determinant metric are explicit in \citet[Sec.~3.1]{woit2021euclidean}. Only that paper's classical geometric review is used here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established finite-dimensional geometry; compactification and affine complexification must be distinguished.

title: The conformal stabilizer and an impossible quotient
notes: The notes write \(\widehat M=SU(2,2)/SO(3,1)\); the next page tentatively suggests \(GL(2,\mathbb C)\times\mathbb R^3\) as stabilizer.
statement: The stabilizer P of a totally null complex two-plane in \(SU(2,2)\) is a real parabolic subgroup of dimension 11. Its Lie algebra is \((\mathfrak{so}(3,1)\oplus\mathbb R)\ltimes\mathbb R^{3,1}\). The compactified real conformal space is \(SU(2,2)/P\), of dimension four. The literal quotient by \(SO(3,1)\) has dimension \(15-6=9\), and the suggested direct product has the wrong group structure.
reconstruction: The parabolic subgroup and its Lie algebra are editorial corrections. Finite central quotients and disconnected components depend on the chosen global conformal action.
fate: The fifteen infinitesimal generators, including the dilation and four special conformal generators missing from the notebook's stabilizer, are explicit in \citet[Sec.~1.1, pp.~245--247]{penrosemaccallum1973twistor}. The dimension and stabilizer corrections follow directly from their action.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The printed homogeneous quotient is false; the corrected parabolic model is standard.

title: SU(2,2) and the conformal spin cover
notes: Equation (2) writes \(SU(2,2)=SO(4,2)\).
statement: Their Lie algebras are isomorphic, but the groups are not equal: \(SU(2,2)\cong\operatorname{Spin}_0(4,2)\) maps two-to-one onto \(SO_0(4,2)\). The effective projective conformal action has additional central identifications. A literal group equality suppresses this covering information.
reconstruction: Connected components, the spin cover and the effective projective quotient replace the informal equality.
fate: The consecutive two-to-one covering relations are stated in \citet[Sec.~1.1, p.~247]{penrosemaccallum1973twistor}; \citet[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean} uses the spin-group identification.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established covering-group relation; equality of Lie algebras must not be confused with equality of groups.

title: The projective null-twistor hypersurface
notes: \(R=\{|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2-|z_3|^2-|z_4|^2=0\}\subset\mathbb CP^3\) is real five-dimensional and preserved by \(SU(2,2)\).
statement: For a nondegenerate Hermitian form h of signature (2,2) on \(\mathbb C^4\), its nonzero null vectors modulo \(\mathbb C^*\) form a smooth real hypersurface \(R\subset\mathbb CP^3\), of real dimension five. Its projective lines are projectivizations of totally h-null two-planes.
reconstruction: Nonzero vectors, projectivization and total nullity clarify the displayed homogeneous equation.
fate: This is the standard real twistor geometry \citep[Sec.~3.3.2]{woit2021euclidean}, already part of the pre-talk Penrose framework \citep{penrosemaccallum1973twistor}. Smoothness and the dimension follow from nondegeneracy of h and projectivization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An exact geometric construction; the ambient projective space is complex but this hypersurface is real.

title: Null two-planes and the U(2) compactification
notes: The manifold of lines entirely contained in R is identified with Minkowski space; the lines are graphs \((z_3,z_4)=U(z_1,z_2)\), \(U\in U(2)\).
statement: In the positive-negative splitting \(\mathbb C^4=\mathbb C^2\oplus\mathbb C^2\), projection of a totally null two-plane to the first summand is injective, hence an isomorphism. The plane is the graph of U, and nullity is exactly \(U^*U=I\). Thus the full manifold of these lines is \(U(2)\cong(S^1\times S^3)/\mathbb Z_2\), the conformal compactification of real Minkowski space, not the affine space itself.
reconstruction: The compactification qualification and elementary graph argument make precise the page's compressed theorem.
fate: The identification with U(2) is explicit in \citet[Sec.~3.3.2, p.~21]{woit2021euclidean}. The distinction between Minkowski space and its compactification is already emphasized by \citet[Sec.~1.1]{penrosemaccallum1973twistor}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established identification. The uncertain initial abbreviation in Theorem 1 is not used to infer a different space.

title: Incidence of twistor lines gives the light cone
notes: Lines in R meeting a fixed line \(L_0\) form a three-dimensional light cone; their intersection points give its generators, and points of R represent light rays.
statement: In a Minkowski graph chart, two twistor lines corresponding to matrices Z and \(Z_0\) meet exactly when \(\det(Z-Z_0)=0\). On the Hermitian real slice this is the ordinary null-separation equation. The fixed null-twistor point determines a null geodesic; varying it over \(L_0\cong\mathbb CP^1\) parametrizes the real celestial two-sphere of null directions through the associated spacetime point.
reconstruction: A local Minkowski chart and the Hermitian real structure distinguish a real light cone from a complex incidence locus.
fate: The determinant/incidence calculation is explicit in \citet[Sec.~3.1, eq.~(3.2) and following paragraphs]{woit2021euclidean}; the real-slice interpretation is classical twistor geometry.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established local conformal geometry, with global compactified identifications at infinity.

title: Conformal inversion and its domain
notes: The conformal group is obtained by adding an inversion \(1/\tau\), with \(\tau\) the Minkowski distance, to Poincare motions.
statement: For the quadratic Minkowski form q, the vector inversion is \(x\mapsto x/q(x)\), defined off \(q(x)=0\) in an affine chart. Together with translations and Lorentz transformations it generates the corresponding extended conformal transformations; compositions yield special conformal transformations and dilations. Its global interpretation uses compactified spacetime, and a single inversion can change components or orientation.
reconstruction: The vector formula, null-cone exclusion and global component qualifications replace the scalar shorthand.
fate: \citet[Sec.~1.1, eq.~(1.2)]{penrosemaccallum1973twistor} gives this inversion and explains why compactification is needed when its null cone goes to infinity.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established conformal transformation; the notebook's reciprocal notation is schematic.

title: Holomorphic connection and curvature
notes:
On an open subset of \(\mathbb C^4\), \(A_\mu(z)\in\mathfrak g\) are holomorphic and \(F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu+[A_\mu,A_
u]\).
statement: For a holomorphic principal G-bundle and a local holomorphic trivialization, \(A=\sum_\mu A_\mu dz^\mu\) is a connection form and \(F=dA+A\wedge A\) its curvature. On overlaps the usual gauge transition rule is required. The displayed coefficients describe one trivializing patch, not an automatic global trivialization of the bundle.
reconstruction: The bundle, patch and transition-function qualifications are supplied.
fate: These are the connection data in the 1978 ambitwistor correspondence, summarized precisely by \citet[Sec.~2]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard holomorphic gauge geometry.

title: The Yang-Mills commutator sign
notes: Equation (6), with the curvature convention in (5), writes \(\sum_\mu(\partial_\mu F_{\mu\nu}+[F_{\mu\nu},A_\mu])=0\).
statement:
For \(F=dA+A\wedge A\), the covariant derivative is \(D=d+[A,\cdot]\). The source-free equation is \(D^\mu F_{\mu
u}=\partial^\mu F_{\mu
u}+[A^\mu,F_{\mu
u}]=0\), with indices raised using the chosen flat complex conformal representative. The printed plus sign and reversed commutator are incompatible with this curvature convention.
reconstruction: The commutator order and metric contraction are corrected explicitly; no alternative sign convention is silently imposed.
fate: The Yang--Mills equation in the geometric correspondence is the conventional covariant equation \citep[Secs.~1--2]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}. The scan explicitly confirms the reversed order, so this is a faithful notebook error.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected equation is standard and gauge covariant.

title: The attributed Landau preference for the S-matrix
notes: Gelfand attributes to Landau the phrase \ru{лагранжиан --- труп} and the view that knowing the S-matrix suffices.
statement: This is a recorded methodological comment, without a defined reconstruction theorem for a Lagrangian from an S-matrix or a uniqueness assertion. Its attribution is the notebook's, not independently authenticated here.
reconstruction: No mathematical quantifiers or historical authentication are supplied beyond the notebook.
fate: No exact mathematical publication is identified with this remark. Searches of the surrounding gauge and factorized-scattering literature give thematic context only; the statement is not made into a technical conjecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: A historical-methodological remark, not an identifiable open problem.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand (attributing a remark to L. D. Landau)

title: The Yang-Mills action and Euler-Lagrange equation
notes: The real equations are said to follow from \(L=\operatorname{tr}\int F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}\,d^4x\).
statement:
On a real oriented flat four-dimensional domain with a nondegenerate invariant bilinear form on \(\mathfrak g\), compactly supported variations of \(S[A]=\int\langle F_{\mu
u},F^{\mu
u}angle\,d^4x\) give \(D_\mu F^{\mu
