u}=0\), up to a nonzero overall normalization. An admissible matrix representation supplies the trace pairing; boundary conditions are needed if variations are not compactly supported.
reconstruction: The invariant pairing, nondegeneracy and boundary/variation conditions are supplied.
fate: This is the classical Yang--Mills variational equation, also used in \citet[Sec.~1, eq.~(1) and surrounding discussion]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}. It yields the corrected commutator order of item 1978-455.9.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established variational identity; it does not validate the reversed commutator printed in (6).

title: The five-dimensional ambitwistor incidence quadric
notes: The notes form \(Q=\{(\ell,\pi):\ell\subset\pi\}\subset\mathbb CP^3\times\mathbb CP^3\), with a dimension glyph transcribed as \(\dim_{\mathbb C}G=5\).
statement: The second factor is the dual projective space: \(Q=F(1,3;\mathbb C^4)=\{([z],[w])\in\mathbb P^3\times\mathbb P^{3*}:w(z)=0\}\). It is a smooth hypersurface of bidegree (1,1), hence complex dimension five. It parametrizes complex null geodesics in compactified complex Minkowski space, with local domains chosen for the connection transform.
reconstruction: The dual projective space and the corrected dimension variable Q are supplied; the dimension glyph in the scan remains palaeographically ambiguous.
fate: The incidence equation and dual space are explicit in \citet[Sec.~2]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}. Beilinson's next-page diagram itself restores the dual star.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established incidence geometry; the arbitrary gauge group G is not asserted to have dimension five.

title: The third formal neighbourhood criterion for full Yang-Mills
notes: The talk credits Witten and independently Yasskin, Isenberg and Green (1978). It identifies solutions with holomorphic G-bundles on Q extending to its third infinitesimal neighbourhood.
statement: Let U be a sufficiently small Stein domain in complex Minkowski space, with every complex null geodesic intersection connected and simply connected. Let \(Q_U\) be the space of null geodesics meeting U. Under the local ambitwistor correspondence, a holomorphic connection solves the full Yang--Mills equations precisely when its associated bundle E, holomorphically trivial on every quadric \(Q_x\cong\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\), extends to the third formal neighbourhood of \(Q_U\) in \(\mathbb P^3\times\mathbb P^{3*}\). With ideal sheaf I, this means the ringed space with structure sheaf \(\mathcal O/I^4\).
reconstruction: The small-domain hypotheses, quadric triviality, dual projective factor and \(I^4\) convention are explicit additions. Triviality is supported by Beilinson's continuation on P000823; it is absent from this page's first statement. Vector bundles or faithful linear realizations of principal bundles are understood with the relevant structure preserved.
fate: Published before the talk: \citet{witten1978interpretation} in August 1978 and \citet{isenbergyasskingreen1978nonselfdual} in October 1978; an earlier first-circulation date was not established here. The exact third-order criterion and domain qualifications are read in \citet[Sec.~2, Theorem~2 and footnote~1]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}, first posted October 2005, published 2006.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An established local holomorphic correspondence for full Yang--Mills fields, not a self-duality-only construction or a new 1979 result.

title: Arbitrary holomorphic connections and bundles before the field equation
notes: The last sentence says all connections correspond to all bundles, without necessarily extending to the third neighbourhood.
statement: On the same admissible local domains, holomorphic connections up to gauge correspond to holomorphic bundles on \(Q_U\) trivial on every \(Q_x\), up to isomorphism preserving the relevant structure. No Yang--Mills equation is imposed at this stage. Arbitrary bundles without the quadric-triviality condition do not satisfy this correspondence.
reconstruction: The local-domain and fibrewise holomorphic-triviality conditions are supplied. Mere vanishing of a Chern class is not substituted for explicit holomorphic triviality. Editorial check: the checked Mason--Skinner review uses a Chern-class shorthand, but \(\mathcal O(1,0)\oplus\mathcal O(-1,0)\) on \(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\) has \(c_1=c_2=0\) and restricts to \(\mathcal O(1)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)\) on a ruling, so it is not holomorphically trivial. The precise fibrewise holomorphic-triviality condition is therefore retained, exactly as P000823 requires; the review's broader shorthand is not used.
fate: This is the pre-equation transform of \citet[Sec.~2, Theorem~1]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}, attributed there to the 1978 papers. Beilinson's intervention supplies the missing condition and construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established conditional correspondence. The unrestricted phrase all bundles is overbroad.

title: The complete-flag double fibration
notes: Let F parametrize line, plane and hyperplane flags in \(\mathbb C^4\); one projection forgets the outer terms and the other forgets the middle plane.
statement: For \(F=F(1,2,3;\mathbb C^4)\), let \(p:F\to X=\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)\) and \(q:F\to Q=F(1,3;4)\). Then \(p^{-1}(x)=\mathbb P(x)\times\mathbb P((\mathbb C^4/x)^*)\cong\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\), whereas \(q^{-1}(\ell,\pi)=\mathbb P(\pi/\ell)\cong\mathbb P^1\). The p-image of a q-fibre is a complex null geodesic.
reconstruction: The two fibre calculations and null-geodesic identification expand the diagram. The local version restricts p to the chosen Minkowski domain.
fate: This is the incidence geometry underlying the pre-talk 1978 transform, reviewed in \citet[Sec.~2]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}. Prior-index 1977-457.1 refers to this same source page and must be an alias, not a prior chronological link.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established flag geometry, with the two different fibre types distinguished.

title: Flatness and horizontal sections along a null curve
notes: A holomorphic bundle with connection becomes canonically trivial on \(\mathbb CP^1\): curvature vanishes by dimension and the fundamental group is zero.
statement: A holomorphic connection restricted to a complex curve is flat, because a holomorphic two-form restricts to zero. On a connected simply connected curve C, evaluation identifies its horizontal sections with every fibre, so \(E|_C\cong\mathcal O_C\otimes H^0_\nabla(C,E)\) canonically. No preferred basis of that vector space is selected. In the local transform C is the null-geodesic intersection with U, not necessarily the full projective line.
reconstruction: Holomorphic rather than arbitrary real connection, connected simply connected domain and the basis-free sense of canonical triviality are supplied.
fate: The horizontal-section construction and simply connected intersections are explicit in \citet[Sec.~2, Theorem~1 and footnote~1]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}. This is part of the same paragraph aliased by prior-index 1977-457.2.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct in the stated holomorphic local setting. It holds for arbitrary such connections and does not impose the Yang--Mills equation.

title: Pullback and descent to the space of null geodesics
notes: Lift \((E,\nabla)\) from \(G(4,2)\) to F and descend it to a holomorphic bundle \(\widetilde E\) on Q because it is trivial on every right-hand fibre.
statement: On an admissible domain U, define \(\widetilde E_l\) to be the vector space of \(\nabla\)-horizontal sections along the null-geodesic intersection \(l\cap U\). Local holomorphic dependence and the absence of monodromy give a holomorphic bundle on \(Q_U\). Equivalently this is descent of \(p^*E\) with its relative flat connection along q.
reconstruction: The admissible local domain, relative connection and holomorphic family qualification are supplied; fibrewise topological triviality by itself is not used as a descent theorem.
fate: This is the forward transform in \citet[Sec.~2, preceding Theorem~1]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}, attributed to Witten and Isenberg--Yasskin--Green in 1978. Prior-index 1977-457.2 is the same page's descent argument.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established local transform for arbitrary holomorphic connections; no field equation is needed for this step.

title: Reverse transform and the quadric-triviality condition
notes: The final line gives \((E,\nabla)\longleftrightarrow\widetilde E\), with \(\widetilde E\) trivial on \(\mathbb CP^1\times\mathbb CP^1\).
statement: For each \(x\in U\), let \(Q_x\) be its quadric of null directions. A holomorphic bundle \(\widetilde E\) trivial on every \(Q_x\), with the same local-domain conditions, reconstructs \(E_x=H^0(Q_x,\widetilde E|_{Q_x})\); incidence of null curves reconstructs the connection. To obtain Yang--Mills, one separately imposes extension to \(\mathcal O/I^4\), as in item 1978-455.13.
reconstruction: The meaning of each quadric, reconstruction fibre and separation of the connection transform from the third-neighbourhood criterion are supplied.
fate: The reverse connection construction and the separate field-equation criterion are \citet[Sec.~2, Theorems~1--2]{masonskinner2006ambitwistor}. Prior-index 1977-457.3 is a duplicate of this final source line, not evidence of an earlier occurrence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An established correspondence. Flatness along one-dimensional null curves alone cannot prove the full Yang--Mills equations.

title: Grading and the two transitivity conditions
notes: A \(\mathbb Z\)-graded algebra has \([\mathfrak g_i,\mathfrak g_j]\subset\mathfrak g_{i+j}\). Bracketing with \(\mathfrak g_{-1}\), respectively \(\mathfrak g_1\), is injective in nonnegative, respectively nonpositive, degree.
statement: For a graded Lie algebra over \(\mathbb C\), each homogeneous piece is a \(\mathfrak g_0\)-module. The displayed maps are \(x\mapsto(v\mapsto[x,v])\); their injectivity means that no nonzero element in the indicated degree centralizes the specified neighbouring component. Classification results require additional assumptions such as finite-dimensional graded pieces and generation by the local part; these are not consequences of the displayed bracket inclusion.
reconstruction: The adjoint maps and missing classification hypotheses are made explicit; the notebook's non-strict degree ranges include degree zero.
fate: \citet[Chapter~I, Sec.~1, Definitions~1--3]{kac1968graded} states these conventions together with finite-dimensionality and local generation. The paper was received 13 February 1968 and published in 1968. Prior alias: 1977-457.4, from this same page.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established graded-algebra definitions; transitivity alone is not the asserted classification theorem.

title: Polynomial vector fields and the degree-zero matrix algebra
notes: \(W_n=\{\sum_i p_i(x)\partial_{x_i}\}\), with \(\deg x_i=1\), \(\deg\partial_{x_i}=-1\); degree zero is the matrix algebra.
statement: For \(n\ge1\), \(W_n=\operatorname{Der}_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\). Its degree-k part consists of vector fields with coefficient polynomials homogeneous of degree \(k+1\), so \((W_n)_{-1}\cong\mathbb C^n\) and \((W_n)_0\cong\mathfrak{gl}_n\), with the usual choice of sign in identifying linear fields with matrices.
reconstruction: The field, derivation algebra and homogeneous-degree convention are expanded.
fate: The polynomial family and grading are explicitly described in \citet[Chapter~III, Sec.~1, (40), type~(1)]{kac1968graded}. Prior alias: the W-family portion of 1977-457.5.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Classical Cartan-type example, already known before the lecture.

title: Divergence-free polynomial vector fields
notes: The second series is the divergence-free vector fields \(S_n\); a possible prime after S is uncertain.
statement: For \(n\ge2\), define \(S_n=\{\sum_i p_i\partial_{x_i}:\sum_i\partial_i p_i=0\}\). Equivalently these vector fields preserve the standard volume form. The inherited degree-zero component is \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\). The one-variable divergence-free space consists only of translations and is not an infinite simple Cartan family.
reconstruction: The divergence formula, volume form and exclusion of the degenerate n=1 case are supplied. The uncertain prime is not resolved as a distinct derived algebra without evidence.
fate: This is \citet[Chapter~III, Sec.~1, type~(2)]{kac1968graded}. Prior alias: the S-family portion of 1977-457.5.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established family with the dimension restriction; the possible prime remains a transcription ambiguity.

title: Hamiltonian polynomial vector fields
notes: The third family is simply named \(H_n\), Hamiltonian vector fields.
statement: On \(\mathbb C^{2n}\), \(n\ge1\), fix \(\omega=\sum_i dq_i\wedge dp_i\). The Hamiltonian vector fields are \(X_f=\sum_i(\partial_{p_i}f\,\partial_{q_i}-\partial_{q_i}f\,\partial_{p_i})\) for polynomial f; constants give the zero field. Equivalently they preserve \(\omega\). A homogeneous polynomial of degree \(k+2\) gives a degree-k field.
reconstruction: The even-dimensional space, symplectic form, quotient by constant Hamiltonians and grading are supplied from the identified standard family.
fate: This is \citet[Chapter~III, Sec.~1, type~(4)]{kac1968graded}. Prior alias: the H-family portion of 1977-457.5.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established polynomial Hamiltonian Lie algebra; the notebook itself does not give this defining formula.

title: Contact polynomial vector fields
notes: The fourth family \(K_n\) preserves a contact structure on \(\mathbb C^{2n+1}\); its grading is explicitly omitted.
statement: For \(n\ge1\), with \(\alpha=dz-\sum_i p_i\,dq_i\), the polynomial contact algebra is \(K_n=\{X:\mathcal L_X\alpha=f\alpha\text{ for some polynomial }f\}\). It preserves the contact distribution, not necessarily the one-form itself. Giving q and p weight one and z weight two yields the usual depth-two contact grading.
reconstruction: The form, conformal preservation condition and weighted grading are supplied. The later depth-one simplification cannot include the full contact grading unchanged.
fate: The contact family and its special filtration appear in \citet[Introduction, p.~1272; Chapter~III, Sec.~1, type~(6), Proposition~18]{kac1968graded}. Prior alias: the K-family portion of 1977-457.5.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established Cartan-type family; omitted grading matters to the scope of the prolongation argument.

title: The four-series classification needs more hypotheses
notes: After the lower grading bound and transitivity conditions, the notes say Cartan's classification gives four series.
statement: An identifiable corrected statement is the classical classification of infinite-dimensional simple Cartan-type algebras under the relevant irreducibility, finite-piece and generation/primitive assumptions, giving vector, divergence-free, Hamiltonian and contact types. The displayed conditions alone neither exclude finite-dimensional examples nor enforce simplicity or irreducibility. Even the general transitive classification includes volume- and symplectic-conformal extensions absent from the four-series shorthand.
reconstruction: The additional assumptions and the distinction between simple and merely transitive classification are explicitly reconstructed from the cited theorem. The exact version intended by Fuchs is not uniquely specified.
fate: \citet[Chapter~III, Theorem~4; Chapter~IV, Theorem~5]{kac1968graded} separates the simple four-family statement from the broader six Cartan types. Prior alias: the classification portion of 1977-457.5. This is known exposition with omitted hypotheses, not an open classification problem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected classical classifications are established; the literal sufficiency of the displayed assumptions is false.

title: The maximal Cartan prolongation and Jacobi symmetry
notes: At depth one, everything is said to be recovered from \(\mathfrak g_{-1},\mathfrak g_0\). Equations (8)--(13) impose symmetry on multilinear maps. The inputs may be arbitrary, simplicity is extra, and infinite dimension is called good luck.
statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and \(\mathfrak h\subset\mathfrak{gl}(V)\) a specified faithful Lie subalgebra. Define \(\mathfrak h^{(k)}=(S^{k+1}V^*\otimes V)\cap(S^kV^*\otimes\mathfrak h)\), with \(\mathfrak h^{(0)}=\mathfrak h\). Then \(V\oplus\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{k\ge1}\mathfrak h^{(k)}\) is the maximal depth-one transitive prolongation. Any other such graded algebra embeds in it; equality is an additional maximality condition. Finite versus infinite type is a precise property of this pair, whereas good luck or usually finite has no specified genericity meaning.
reconstruction: Finite-dimensionality, a faithful specified action and maximality are supplied. Recoverability of an arbitrary graded algebra from its nonpositive part is corrected to an embedding into the maximal prolongation.
fate: The classical prolongation framework predates the talk; \citet{guilleminquillensternberg1967infinite} studies infinite-type irreducible inputs. The exact tensor-intersection definition is read in \citet[Definition~2.1]{fuhwang2010prolongation}. Prior alias: 1977-457.6. No unseen rank-one criterion from P000826 is attributed to the available pages.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established construction. The notebook's unrestricted uniqueness and informal genericity wording require these qualifications.

title: The inductive bracket in the prolongation
notes: To define \([\alpha,\beta]\), specify \([[\alpha,\beta],\delta]\) for \(\delta\in\mathfrak g_{-1}\); Jacobi reduces it to lower degrees.
statement: For homogeneous positive-degree elements X,Y in the maximal prolongation and \(v\in V\), define \([[X,Y],v]=[X,[Y,v]]-[Y,[X,v]]\). Transitivity gives uniqueness. Existence and Jacobi follow by realizing the symmetric tensors as homogeneous polynomial vector fields and using their ordinary commutator; the symmetry conditions are precisely those needed to remain in the prolongation.
reconstruction: The explicit Jacobi identity and the polynomial-vector-field realization justify existence as well as uniqueness. The latter is explanatory reconstruction, not the additional construction on the missing following page.
fate: This is the standard prolongation bracket associated to the tensor definition \citep[Definition~2.1 and discussion of symmetry algebras]{fuhwang2010prolongation}, within the pre-1979 Cartan framework. Prior alias: 1977-457.7.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established algebraic construction; no unsolved bracket-definition problem remains.

title: The loop algebra twisted by an involution
notes: An involution \(\tau\) gives \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g_+\oplus\mathfrak g_-\), and the algebra is \(\cdots\oplus\mathfrak g_-t^{-1}\oplus\mathfrak g_+\oplus\mathfrak g_-t\oplus\mathfrak g_+t^2\oplus\cdots\).
statement: For a complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) and an automorphism \(\tau^2=1\), let \(\mathfrak g_\pm\) be its eigenspaces. Then \([\mathfrak g_\epsilon,\mathfrak g_\delta]\subset\mathfrak g_{\epsilon\delta}\), and \(L(\mathfrak g,\tau)=\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_{(-1)^k}t^k\) is a Lie subalgebra of \(\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C[t,t^{-1}]\). This is the centreless twisted loop algebra; adding an affine central extension and a derivation is separate data.
reconstruction: The automorphism rather than vector-space involution hypothesis, eigenspace brackets and distinction from the full affine algebra are supplied.
fate: \citet[Chapter~II, Sec.~6, Definition~9 and following construction, pp.~1292--1293]{kac1968graded} gives the general finite-order construction. Prior alias: the construction in 1977-457.17.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established loop construction; no affine central generator or derivation is printed in this source segment.

title: Negative transpose on sl(3)
notes: The example is \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3\), with \(\tau\) described as reflection across the diagonal, negative transposition.
statement: The map \(\tau(X)=-X^{\mathsf T}\) is an involutive Lie algebra automorphism of \(\mathfrak{sl}_3(\mathbb C)\). Its fixed algebra is \(\mathfrak{so}_3(\mathbb C)\), dimension three; its negative eigenspace consists of symmetric traceless matrices, dimension five. Alternating these spaces gives the standard twisted \(A_2\) loop construction.
reconstruction: The minus sign is essential: ordinary transpose is an anti-automorphism. Eigenspaces and the centreless qualification are supplied.
fate: This is the order-two outer-automorphism case of \citet[Chapter~II, Sec.~6, Lemmas~21--22]{kac1968graded}. Prior alias: the explicit example within 1977-457.17.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established example; the phrase reflection is interpreted using the page's explicit negative-transpose parenthesis.

title: A period-three one-dimensional graded bracket
notes: For basis elements \(\varepsilon_i\), \(i\in\mathbb Z\), the bracket is \([\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_j]=a_{ij}\varepsilon_{i+j}\), where \(a_{ij}\in\{-1,0,1\}\) is congruent to \(j-i\) modulo three.
statement: The literal rule defines a Lie algebra isomorphic to \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\otimes\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]\). With \([H,E]=2E\), \([H,F]=-2F\), \([E,F]=H\), an explicit isomorphism is \(\varepsilon_{3k}\mapsto\frac12Hz^k\), \(\varepsilon_{3k+1}\mapsto Ez^k\), \(\varepsilon_{3k-1}\mapsto\frac12Fz^k\). Checking the nine residue pairs verifies the structure constants and Jacobi. This algebra is graded-simple for this grading, but is not simple as an ungraded Lie algebra: evaluation at z=1 has a proper nonzero kernel.
reconstruction: The basis isomorphism and the graded-versus-ungraded simplicity distinction are supplied. This particular grading is not generated by degrees -1,0,1, so Kac's local-generation convention cannot be silently applied to it.
fate: The loop-algebra setting and the distinction between homogeneous simplicity and arbitrary ideals are explicit in \citet[Introduction; Chapter~II, Sec.~6, Proposition~10]{kac1968graded}. The displayed basis identification is an elementary check of the notes' exact coefficients, not a claimed later discovery. Prior alias: 1977-457.18.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: An identifiable centreless loop algebra with an unusual grading. Calling it simple without specifying homogeneous ideals is false.

title: The unspecified three-algebra and two-construction exhaustion claims
notes: There are said to be three simple algebras with the displayed one-dimensional pieces, but only one is written. The final line says these two constructions exhaust everything up to grading.
statement: No complete list of three, definition of simplicity, finite-growth bound, support condition, local-generation hypothesis or intended equivalence of gradings is supplied. The literal universal claim about all graded Lie algebras is false. A precise classical finite-growth classification exists under additional hypotheses, but the absent pages prevent identification of the exact quantified version intended here.
reconstruction: The missing quantifiers are identified rather than supplied as historical facts; the unseen P000826--P000828 could have contained qualifications, but that is not evidence of their content.
fate: \citet[Introduction and Chapter~III, Theorem~4]{kac1968graded} classifies irreducible graded-simple finite-growth algebras with its explicit conventions. It does not justify dropping those assumptions. Prior alias: 1977-457.19. No definite open classification problem is inferred from the incomplete list.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The literal scope is unidentified. Established classifications provide context, not proof of an unrestricted exhaustion claim.

title: The real N=1 super-Poincare algebra
notes: The notes list four \(P_m\), six \(L_{mn}\), and two-component \(Q_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}\), with \(\{Q_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta}\}=2\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_m\), zero same-chirality anticommutators and \([P,Q]=0\); the dimension is \((10,4)\).
statement: Let \(\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)\), \(\sigma^m=(I,\sigma^1,\sigma^2,\sigma^3)\). Extend \(\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)\) by a real Majorana odd module, written as conjugate Weyl modules. The only nonzero odd brackets are the displayed mixed anticommutators; Lorentz generators act in \((\tfrac12,0)\oplus(0,\tfrac12)\). Together with the Poincar\'e brackets this is a real Lie superalgebra of superdimension \(10|4\). The complexification has the corresponding two independent complex Weyl modules.
reconstruction: The Majorana reality condition, metric convention and Lorentz action complete shorthand in the notes. A bar/dot lost in the second bracket display is restored mathematically, not claimed as visible handwriting. The total 14 counts real dimensions.
fate: Already standard in \citet[Sec.~2, Eqs.~(2.2)--(2.3)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}; publication predates the talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Hermitian matrices and the Lorentz double cover
notes: The vector \(x\) is written as \(X=x^m\sigma_m=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}x_0+x_3&x_1-ix_2\\x_1+ix_2&x_0-x_3\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). The transformation \(A\mapsto X^+AX\), \(X\in SL(2,\mathbb C)\), preserves the determinant.
statement: The real vector space \(\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)\) has quadratic form \(\det X=(x^0)^2-\sum_{i=1}^3(x^i)^2\). The action \(X\mapsto gXg^\dagger\) induces the surjection \(SL(2,\mathbb C)\to SO^+(1,3)\) with kernel \(\{\pm I\}\). The fundamental and conjugate Weyl modules carry the invariant alternating spinor forms \(\varepsilon_{12}=-\varepsilon_{21}=1\).
reconstruction: The notes reuse \(X\) for both a vector matrix and a group element. We separate these roles. The identity component and double-cover qualification are supplied.
fate: The spinor conventions are reviewed in \citet[Appendix]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}; this is classical Lorentz geometry.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Constructing a superalgebra from its even algebra and odd module
notes: At the end of P000830 the speaker starts with \(\mathfrak g_0\) and its module \(\mathfrak g_1\), seeks a bracket on their sum, and on P000831 says it is unique in the present case.
statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, a Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g_0\), a \(\mathfrak g_0\)-module \(V\), and an equivariant symmetric map \(b:S^2V\to\mathfrak g_0\) define a Lie superalgebra precisely when \(b(v,w)\cdot u+b(w,u)\cdot v+b(u,v)\cdot w=0\). For the minimal supertranslation algebra, require translation-invariant odd generators and a nonzero Lorentz-equivariant mixed Weyl bracket into the translation module. That map is unique up to scale; fixing its coefficient as \(2\) fixes the stated normalization.
reconstruction: We supply the odd Jacobi condition and limit uniqueness to the stated modules and target. Unrestricted extensions, including central charges, are not unique.
fate: The required graded Jacobi framework appears in \citet[Sec.~2]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Extended supersymmetry and internal indices
notes: Equation (2) introduces \(Q^i_\alpha\) and \(\{Q^i_\alpha,\bar Q^j_{\dot\beta}\}=2\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_m\delta^{ij}\), with \(i,j\) internal-symmetry indices.
statement: For \(N\) Weyl supercharges and their conjugates, the displayed relation defines the central-charge-free extended supertranslation algebra; same-chirality brackets vanish. Internal unitary transformations act on the multiplicity index. More general \(N>1\) supersymmetry algebras may have \(\{Q^i_\alpha,Q^j_\beta\}=\varepsilon_{\alpha\beta}Z^{ij}\), where \(Z^{ij}=-Z^{ji}\) are central.
reconstruction: The central-charge-free restriction is essential; the last clause records the scope of the classification, not an extra assertion made in the notebook.
fate: \citet[Sec.~1, Eqs.~(1.1)--(1.7)]{haaglopuszanskisohnius1975supersymmetries} already included central charges in 1975 (received 15 November 1974).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The no-go theorem is a statement about scattering symmetries
notes: The notes call this a nontrivial mixing of internal and spatial symmetry, write \ru{протон + антипротон = импульс}, and say ordinary Lie algebras cannot do it because of a theorem.
statement: Under the hypotheses of a nontrivial relativistic scattering theory with a mass gap, finitely many particle types at each mass, and sufficiently regular additive symmetry generators, even scattering symmetries split into Poincar\'e and commuting internal parts; graded extensions can possess the displayed spinorial generators. This is not a theorem forbidding arbitrary abstract Lie-algebra extensions or semidirect products.
reconstruction: The scattering hypotheses are restored from the relevant no-go/supersymmetry theorem. The proton phrase is an analogy for the spinor anticommutator, not a particle-reaction identity.
fate: \citet[Secs.~1--2, especially limitations on p.~258]{haaglopuszanskisohnius1975supersymmetries} gives the precise scope.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Superspace and the finite superfield expansion
notes: The notes adjoin \(\theta^\alpha,\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}\) to \(x^m\), impose anticommutation, and expand \(\varphi=A+\theta\psi+\bar\theta\bar\psi+\theta\theta B+\bar\theta\bar\theta C+\theta\sigma\bar\theta h+\cdots+\theta\theta\bar\theta\bar\theta D\).
statement: The complexified function sheaf of flat superspace is \(C^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3};\mathbb C)\otimes\Lambda(\theta^1,\theta^2,\bar\theta^{\dot1},\bar\theta^{\dot2})\). Every superfunction has a unique expansion in its \(2^4=16\) exterior monomials; its total odd degree is at most four. The quadratic mixed term is \(\theta\sigma^m\bar\theta\,h_m(x)\), with a vector index \(m\), and the cubic terms are included in the ellipsis. Translations act by \(P_m=-i\partial_m\); Lorentz transformations also act on the spinor coordinates.
reconstruction: We distinguish a sheaf of superfunctions from ordinary points with numeric anticommuting coordinates. The ambiguous manuscript \(\alpha\) on \(\sigma,h\) must be a vector index in the mixed term.
fate: See \citet[Sec.~3(a)--(b), Eq.~(3.12)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields} for this pre-talk construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Odd differential operators realize the supertranslation brackets
notes: Equation (5) gives \(Q_\alpha=-i\partial_\alpha-(\sigma^m\bar\theta)_\alpha\partial_m\) and \(\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}=i\bar\partial_{\dot\alpha}+(\theta\sigma^m)_{\dot\alpha}\partial_m\). The next page says these realize (1).
statement: Use left odd derivatives on the exterior algebra and \(P_m=-i\partial_m\). The displayed odd operators satisfy \(\{Q_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta}\}=-2i\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\beta}\partial_m=2\sigma^m_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_m\), while \(\{Q,Q\}=\{\bar Q,\bar Q\}=0\) and they commute with all translations.
reconstruction: The side of odd differentiation is specified; changing it without changing signs changes the formulas. The assertion follows directly by the graded Leibniz rule.
fate: This superspace realization predates 1979; see \citet[Sec.~3]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Supertranslations on coordinates
notes: Equation (6) shifts \(\theta\) by \(\lambda\), \(\bar\theta\) by \(\bar\lambda\), and \(x^m\) by \(i(\theta\sigma^m\bar\lambda-\lambda\sigma^m\bar\theta)\).
statement: For constant odd parameters \(\lambda,\bar\lambda\) anticommuting with all odd coordinates, this polynomial transformation, together with ordinary translations, gives the supertranslation group law. In infinitesimal form \(\delta_\lambda\theta=\lambda\), \(\delta_\lambda\bar\theta=\bar\lambda\), and \(\delta_\lambda x^m=i(\theta\sigma^m\bar\lambda-\lambda\sigma^m\bar\theta)\).
reconstruction: All odd parameters anticommute mutually. Formula (6) is interpreted in the functor-of-points sense; its body is an ordinary spacetime translation.
fate: Compare \citet[Sec.~3(a), Eq.~(3.4)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}, with the chosen sign convention.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The commutator closes on translations, with a factor correction
notes: After saying that doing two transformations gives a pure translation, equation (7) writes \((\delta_\lambda\delta_\mu-\delta_\mu\delta_\lambda)x^m=i(\mu\sigma^m\bar\lambda-\lambda\sigma^m\bar\mu)\). The scan has no factor \(2\).
statement: For the preceding infinitesimal variations, treated as even derivations with fixed parameters, \([\delta_\lambda,\delta_\mu]x^m=2i(\lambda\sigma^m\bar\mu-\mu\sigma^m\bar\lambda)\) and \([\delta_\lambda,\delta_\mu]\theta=[\delta_\lambda,\delta_\mu]\bar\theta=0\). Reversing commutator order reverses the sign but never removes the factor two. An ordinary composition of two supertranslations still shifts the odd coordinates; it is their commutator that is purely translational.
reconstruction: This is an explicit algebraic correction of the notebook, independently checked by applying each variation to equation (6). It is not a transcription error.
fate: Closure with coefficient two is already displayed in \citet[Eq.~(1.2)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: A scalar superfield transforms by pullback
notes: Equation (8) is \(\varphi'(x',\theta',\bar\theta')=\varphi(x,\theta,\bar\theta)\); the component transformations are described as complicated.
statement: For a superspace automorphism \(T\), a scalar superfield has the passive transformation \(\varphi'=\varphi\circ T^{-1}\). Expanding in the exterior generators determines its component transformations uniquely and mixes even and odd component fields. This is a transformation law, not an invariance assertion \(\varphi' =\varphi\) at fixed coordinates.
reconstruction: Passive and active conventions are distinguished to avoid a sign ambiguity in component variations.
fate: Compare \citet[Sec.~3(b), Eqs.~(3.13)--(3.14)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Chiral coordinates and left-right decomposition
notes: Equations (9), (11) define \(x_L=x+i\theta\sigma\bar\theta\), \(x_R=x-i\theta\sigma\bar\theta\), with \(\delta x_L=2i\theta\sigma\bar\lambda\) and \(\delta x_R=-2i\lambda\sigma\bar\theta\). P000833 records their sum and difference.
statement: In the same Grassmann conventions, the infinitesimal transformation of \((x_L,\theta)\) depends only on \((x_L,\theta)\) and the parameters; likewise for \((x_R,\bar\theta)\). Moreover \(x=(x_L+x_R)/2\) and \(x_L-x_R=2i\theta\sigma\bar\theta\). These are coordinate identities on complexified superspace. For finite odd shifts the induced \(x_L,x_R\) transformations also contain terms quadratic in the shift parameters.
reconstruction: The formulas for \(\delta\) are explicitly infinitesimal, as the notebook says; they must not be read as complete finite transformation formulas.
fate: The equivalent chiral changes of realization are in \citet[Sec.~3(a), Eqs.~(3.8)--(3.9)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The chiral multiplet and its auxiliary component
notes: The special \ru{киральные} fields are \(\varphi_L(x_L,\theta)=A(x_L)+\theta^\alpha\psi_\alpha(x_L)+\theta^\alpha\theta_\alpha F(x_L)\).
statement: A chiral scalar superfield is a superfunction independent of \(\bar\theta\) in the coordinates \((x_L,\theta,\bar\theta)\), equivalently annihilated by the corresponding covariant odd derivatives. Its expansion has exactly a complex scalar \(A\), a Weyl spinor \(\psi\), and a complex scalar auxiliary coefficient \(F\). This off-shell construction is closed under the global supersymmetry action; no field equation or gravitational coupling is asserted.
reconstruction: The normalization of \(\psi\) and \(F\) is conventional; factors such as \(\sqrt2\) can be absorbed into them. The covariant-derivative formulation is a modern equivalent definition.
fate: Already in \citet[Sec.~3(c)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: A continuous local Lie bracket on sections
notes: For a smooth manifold \(M\) and vector bundle \(E\), the notes give a bilinear skew bracket on \(\Gamma^\infty(E)\), satisfying Jacobi, continuous for uniform convergence of every derivative on compact sets, and \(\operatorname{supp}[s,t]\subset\operatorname{supp}s\cap\operatorname{supp}t\).
statement: Let \(M\) be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold and \(E\to M\) a finite-rank smooth real vector bundle. A local Lie algebra structure is a jointly continuous \(\mathbb R\)-bilinear Lie bracket on the Fr\'echet space \(\Gamma^\infty(E)\) with the displayed support property. Restriction gives a sheaf of Lie algebras. No \(C^\infty(M)\)-bilinearity or fixed global differential order is assumed.
reconstruction: Second countability and the usual smooth-section topology are understood; the notes' differential algebra here means a local Lie algebra, not a differential field.
fate: This is the setting of \citet[Sec.~1, Russian pp.~58--59]{kirillov1976local}, published in 1976; received 25 November 1975.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Locality gives differential expressions; rank one gives first order
notes: In a local trivialization the bracket is written \([f,g]=\sum c_{kl}(x)\partial^k f\partial^l g\).
statement: A continuous support-local bilinear operation on smooth sections is locally a bidifferential operator: on every sufficiently small relatively compact chart only finitely many derivatives occur. For a Lie bracket on a line bundle, Jacobi and skew symmetry reduce its order to at most one in each argument. In a local frame it therefore has the form \([f,g]=\Lambda(df,dg)+fE(g)-gE(f)\), where \(\Lambda\) is a bivector and \(E\) a vector field, subject to the Jacobi identity.
reconstruction: The locally finite order and the later first-order restriction are separated. The displayed arbitrary multi-index sum alone does not assert infinite differential order.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2, Lemmas~1--2, Russian pp.~59--60]{kirillov1976local} proves both reductions. The author's \citet[p.~268]{kirillov1977errata} corrects the coordinate Jacobi identities of Lemma~3; it does not withdraw the finite-order and first-order statements of Lemmas~1--2 used here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The scope of Kirillov's rank-one classification
notes: The theorem says rank-one differential Lie algebras are essentially Poisson or contact; the phrase \ru{Все остальные формально изоморфны} follows the two models.
statement: The characteristic distribution generated locally by \(E\) and \(\Lambda^\sharp T^*M\) has integral leaves. On a transitive leaf the local Lie structure is of contact type in odd dimension and of locally conformally symplectic type in positive even dimension; after a local change of line-bundle frame the even model is symplectic Poisson. Rank-zero leaves and singular changes of leaf dimension are permitted for a general local Lie algebra. The theorem is leafwise and local, and does not identify every global bracket on every line bundle with one fixed flat model.
reconstruction: Transitivity, localization and line-bundle changes of frame repair the overly compressed assertion. This is a classification of rank-one bundles, not bundles of arbitrary rank.
fate: See \citet[Sec.~2, Theorem~1; Secs.~3--4, Theorems~2--3]{kirillov1976local}; all precede the session.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The standard Poisson model
notes: Case (a) takes \(M=\mathbb R^{2n}\) and \([f,g]=\sum_i(f_{x_i}g_{y_i}-f_{y_i}g_{x_i})\).
statement: On \(\mathbb R^{2n}\), the inverse bivector to the constant symplectic form gives this Lie bracket on smooth functions. It is a first-order bidifferential operation in each input, obeys the Leibniz rule, and is transitive for \(n\ge1\).
reconstruction: The symplectic interpretation explains the even-dimensional model; its local nature is essential in the preceding classification.
fate: This is the flat model in \citet[Sec.~3]{kirillov1976local}, not a new 1979 result.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The contact model has a sign error in the notebook
notes: Case (b) writes \(X_i=\partial_{x_i}\), \(Y_i=\partial_{y_i}+x_i\partial_z\), \(Z=\partial_z\), and \([f,g]=fZg-gZf+\sum_i(X_if\,Y_ig-X_ig\,Y_if)\). Both plus signs are legible.
statement: With the displayed plus sign in \(Y_i\), the operation fails Jacobi already for one pair: \([x,y]=1\), \([y,z]=y\), \([z,x]=-2x\), whence \([x,[y,z]]+[y,[z,x]]+[z,[x,y]]=2\). A consistent contact bracket is obtained by replacing \(Y_i\) with \(\partial_{y_i}-x_i\partial_z\), retaining the rest of the displayed formula. It corresponds to the contact form \(dz+\sum_i x_i\,dy_i\) in these conventions.
reconstruction: The sign replacement is an editorial mathematical emendation, not a claim about what the writer wrote. The explicit Jacobi obstruction and corrected bracket are checked in the critical annotations and the reproducible symbolic calculation.
fate: Contact local Lie algebras themselves are classical; compare \citet[Sec.~4, Theorem~3]{kirillov1976local}. The notebook's literal formula is refuted directly.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the intended contact model is established; the literal notebook formula is false. No open problem is created by the error.

title: The diagram of higher-rank classification gaps
notes: A diagram has the rank-one row marked Kirillov, the one-dimensional-base/rank-two point marked \ru{10 алгебр Ритта}, and a region marked question marks and \ru{есть только правдоподобная версия}.
statement: The diagram distinguishes base dimension from fiber rank. It supplies no candidate brackets, equivalence relation, transitivity condition, or formal versus smooth category for the region of question marks. Consequently no definite higher-rank conjecture can be reconstructed. Ritt's rank-two point can be identified separately with the formal one-derivation classification.
reconstruction: The count is corrected in item 1978-459.11. The unspecified ``plausible version'' is retained as an unresolved identification rather than turned into a modern classification problem.
fate: Searches of Kirillov's original paper and Ritt/Cassidy material located the two named theories, but no precise conjecture matching this diagram. \citet[Sec.~5, point~6]{kirillov1976local} explicitly distinguishes the greater complexity of higher-rank bundles.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the intended higher-rank statement is not identifiable from the surviving notes; this is not evidence that a specified problem remains open.

title: Formal pseudodifferential symbols as an infinite-component Lie algebra
notes: The series \(\sigma=\sum_{i\ge1}a_i\xi^{-(i+1)}\) is supplied with a noncommutative product determined by \([\xi,x]=1\); its commutator is said to be a differential Lie algebra on a one-dimensional base with infinite-dimensional fiber.
statement: Let \((F,\partial)\) be a commutative differential algebra of characteristic zero. Formal symbols with orders bounded above have associative multiplication \((a\xi^m)\circ(b\xi^n)=\sum_{j\ge0}\binom mj a\,\partial^jb\,\xi^{m+n-j}\). Each coefficient is a finite sum. The negative-order symbols, and also the order-at-most-minus-two tail actually displayed, are closed under commutator. The relation \([\xi,a]=\partial a\) specializes to \([\xi,x]=1\) when \(\partial x=1\).
reconstruction: We specify formal multiplication and coefficientwise completion. The possibly duplicated extra \(a\) after \(a_i\) is not assigned mathematical significance. The index \(i\ge1\) is preserved; adding a \(\xi^{-1}\) coefficient gives the full usual Volterra Lie algebra. This infinite-rank example lies outside the finite-rank smooth-bundle hypotheses.
fate: The same construction is in \citet[Secs.~3--4, Russian p.~42]{lebedevmanin1979volterra}, received 10 November 1978 and published in 1979. Receipt does not establish public circulation; this passage introduces a formal-symbol construction, not the later Hamiltonian theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the formal symbol algebra and its commutator are established. The analytic operator realization and convergence are not asserted here.

title: Formal differential power series and the required completion
notes: The notes introduce a characteristic-zero differential field, independent jets \(y_i,y_i',\ldots\), and \(F[\![ y_1,\ldots,y_m]\!]=\bigoplus_{\tau\ge0}F_\tau\). The next page writes \(U=\sum_kP_k\) with each \(P_k\) homogeneous in all jets.
statement: Give every jet \(\partial^j y_i\) total degree one. Let \(F_\tau\) be the space of differential polynomials homogeneous of degree \(\tau\), each containing finitely many monomials. The formal differential power-series algebra used here is the degree completion \(\prod_{\tau\ge0}F_\tau\). Differentiation preserves degree and continuous substitution of series with zero constant term is defined degree by degree.
reconstruction: The direct sum in the displayed definition would give only differential polynomials, so it is replaced by the completed product. The finite-monomial condition at each degree prevents an additional unsupported completion in jet order.
fate: This formal category is explained in \citet[Ch.~III, Sec.~1, pp.~263--264]{cassidy1979differential}, restating Ritt's 1950 formal theory.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Formal differential group laws
notes: A differential group is given by \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)\) in the jets of \(u,v\), with \(U(u,0)=u\), \(U(0,v)=v\), and \(U(U(u,v),w)=U(u,U(v,w))\).
statement: Over a characteristic-zero differential field, a formal differential group law of dimension \(m\) is an \(m\)-tuple of degree-completed differential series in two \(m\)-tuples, with linear term \(u+v\), satisfying the identities shown. Composition includes all formal derivatives of substituted series. The formal inverse is obtained recursively by total degree. Isomorphisms are invertible formal differential substitutions fixing zero, not arbitrary changes of a smooth infinite-dimensional manifold.
reconstruction: The inverse and equivalence category are made explicit. Here ``dimension'' counts independent differential coordinates, not the infinitely many jet variables as ordinary coordinates.
fate: \citet[Ch.~III, Secs.~1--3]{cassidy1979differential} restates the formal groups and their Lie correspondence from Ritt's 1950--1951 papers.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The substitution group and tensor-density modules
notes: The basic group \(\Pi\) has \(U(u,v)=u+v(x+u)=u+v+uv'+\tfrac12u^2v''+\cdots\). The notes also introduce the additive group \(A_h\) of expressions \(u(x)(dx)^{-h}\).
statement: Near the identity, write a formal change of variable as \(\phi_u(x)=x+u(x)\). Composition \(\phi_v\circ\phi_u\) has parameter \(u+\sum_{j\ge0}u^j\partial^jv/j!\), a well-defined differential series. The skew bilinear term is \(uv'-vu'\). For scalar \(h\), tensor densities of weight \(-h\) form an additive module: the pullback action of \(\phi\) is \(a(x)(dx)^{-h}\mapsto a(\phi(x))(\phi'(x))^{-h}(dx)^{-h}\), with binomial powers expanded formally near \(\phi'=1\).
reconstruction: The density action is supplied to explain the extension language. These are formal changes near the identity, not transformations which literally fix every value of \(x\). Associativity follows from composition.
fate: The substitution formal group and its Lie algebra occur in \citet[Ch.~IV, Sec.~1, Theorem~5]{cassidy1979differential}; the density action is the explicit interpretation of the notebook's notation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Ritt's rank-two classification has thirteen types
notes: The diagram says ``10 algebras of Ritt''. Theorem~2 says that when the base has dimension one and the fiber has dimension two, all the groups are extensions of \(\Pi\) by \(A_h\).
statement: Over a universal ordinary differential field of characteristic zero, the differential Lie-algebra structures on its two-dimensional additive vector group, up to differential isomorphism, fall into thirteen types: three finite and ten substitutional types, with parameter families inside some types. The corresponding formal differential-group laws are classified through Ritt's Lie correspondence. They are not all extensions of a substitution group by an abelian density module: the additive two-coordinate group has no nonabelian substitution quotient, while one substitutional type is \(\Pi\times\Pi\). Many remaining substitutional types do have an abelian differential ideal and a substitutional quotient, with nontrivial cocycles possible.
reconstruction: This is a correction of the count and universal quantifier, with the formal category and the universal differential-field setting used by Cassidy restored. Descent to an arbitrary coefficient field is not asserted. No classification of all smooth rank-two bundles over arbitrary curves is inferred. A list of thirteen types is a list of families, not thirteen isomorphism classes.
fate: The original is \citet[pp.~491--519]{ritt1951groups} (metadata checked); the full classification list and exceptions were read in \citet[Introduction, p.~247; Ch.~IV, Sec.~2, pp.~268--269; Sec.~3]{cassidy1979differential}. Cassidy was received 15 September 1976 and published in 1979; Ritt's result was published in 1951.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: the formal one-derivation classification in the stated universal-field setting is established; the unqualified extension statement in the source is false.

title: Regular webs and the needed general-position condition
notes: A web is a finite number of foliations with transverse leaves on a manifold.
statement: For the codimension-one results below, a regular holomorphic \(d\)-web near \(0\in\mathbb C^n\) is a family of submersions \(u_1,\ldots,u_d\), taken up to one-variable reparametrization, whose level sets define the foliations. Every subset of at most \(n\) covectors among \(du_1(0),\ldots,du_d(0)\) is linearly independent. Shrink the neighborhood so that this holds everywhere. Pairwise transversality alone is insufficient when \(n>2\).
reconstruction: The holomorphic germ category and full conormal general position are supplied for the precise theorems, rather than attributed to the notebook's single word ``transverse''.
fate: The contemporary formulation is in \citet[Sec.~1]{beauville1980tissus}, a February 1979 lecture published in 1980; compare the exact hypotheses in \citet[Sec.~1.1]{trepreau2006algebrisation}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Incidence webs from a projective variety
notes: For \(X\subset\mathbb P^n\), \(\dim X=m\), \(\deg X=d\), the notes take the open set of complementary planes meeting \(X\) in \(d\) distinct points. They call \(\{H:\exists i,\ P_i\in H\}\) a leaf and say the foliation has codimension one.
statement: Let \(X\) be a reduced pure \(m\)-dimensional projective variety over \(\mathbb C\), and let \(U\subset\operatorname{Gr}(n-m+1,n+1)\) consist of projective \((n-m)\)-planes meeting \(X\) transversely in \(d\) distinct smooth points. Near \(H_0\in U\), label these intersection points holomorphically as \(p_i(H)\). Each map \(p_i:U\to X\) is locally a submersion, and its fibers form a foliation of codimension \(m\). The \(i\)-th leaf through \(H_0\) consists locally of planes containing the fixed point \(p_i(H_0)\). The existential quantifier in the notes gives the union of \(d\) leaves, not a single leaf.
reconstruction: Grassmannian convention, smooth transverse intersections, local labels and the correct codimension are supplied. Global labeling can fail by permutation monodromy. Codimension one applies only after the next page's specialization \(m=1\).
fate: This incidence construction is described in \citet[Sec.~2, pp.~105--106; Sec.~11]{beauville1980tissus}; the erroneous codimension and union are repaired directly from the incidence dimensions.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Gelfand's Crofton formula and its normalization
notes: \ru{Крофтона формула}: the length of a curve is the average number of its intersections with a line, averaged using an invariant measure.
statement: For a compact piecewise \(C^1\) immersed plane curve \(\gamma\), counted with parametrization multiplicity, put \(N(\theta,p)=\#\{t:\gamma(t)\cdot(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)=p\}\) for almost all \((\theta,p)\). With unoriented lines represented by \(0\le\theta<\pi\), \(p\in\mathbb R\), one has \(\operatorname{length}(\gamma)=\tfrac12\int_0^\pi\int_{\mathbb R}N(\theta,p)\,dp\,d\theta\). The invariant measure is infinite on all lines, so ``average'' means an integral with a fixed normalization, not a uniform probability distribution on the entire line space.
reconstruction: The coefficient and regularity are supplied. Applying the one-dimensional change-of-variables formula to each projection gives \(\int N(\theta,p)dp=\int|\gamma'(t)\cdot n_\theta|dt\); integrating \(\theta\) gives \(2\int|\gamma'|dt\), independently checking the normalization.
fate: The formula is classical; \citet[Introduction and Sec.~3, pp.~79--80]{linwang1996integral} recalls its nineteenth-century origin and integral-geometric interpretation. That later paper is a checked source for the classical attribution, not the fate of a new 1979 question.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: When can a planar three-web be made parallel?
notes: Gelfand asks when three transverse planar foliations can be straightened; two always can. The answer in the notes is hexagonality, dated approximately 1927, with an infinitesimal closed-path diagram and a curvature analogy.
statement: For a regular holomorphic planar three-web, local equivalence to \(x=\mathrm{const}\), \(y=\mathrm{const}\), \(x+y=\mathrm{const}\) is equivalent to closure of every sufficiently small web hexagon. Equivalently, choose defining forms \(\omega_1+\omega_2+\omega_3=0\) and the unique connection form \(\gamma\) satisfying \(d\omega_i=\omega_i\wedge\gamma\); the condition is \(d\gamma=0\). The corresponding statement holds in the regular smooth real category. This is parallelizability, a stronger requirement than merely obtaining three families of nonparallel straight lines.
reconstruction: The standard hexagonal closure, rather than an inferred exact traversal of the faint diagram, is used. The connection formulation makes the notebook's curvature analogy precise. No general planar three-web linearizability conjecture is substituted for this old problem.
fate: Thomsen's 1927 result is explicitly recalled in \citet[Sec.~1, pp.~103--104]{beauville1980tissus}. The notebook itself gives both question and answer.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: solved in the stated parallelizability sense; the hexagon criterion is classical.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The dual web of a projective curve
notes: The notes now put \(m=1\), take a projective curve \(X\), and construct a codimension-one web on the open subset of \(\check{\mathbb P}^{n}\) consisting of transverse hyperplanes.
statement: Let \(C\subset\mathbb P^n\) be a smooth irreducible nondegenerate complex projective curve of degree \(d\). On a sufficiently small open set of hyperplanes with \(d\) distinct transverse intersections in linear general position, label the intersection maps \(p_i\). The hypersurfaces \(p_i(H)=p_i(H_0)\) are pieces of hyperplanes in the dual projective space, giving a linear \(d\)-web. The regularity and general-position open set is part of the construction.
reconstruction: Smoothness, nondegeneracy and the choice of a regular open set avoid unsupported assertions about singular intersections or degenerate curves. The specialization is distinct from the general-codimension construction.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2]{beauville1980tissus} gives exactly this construction; see also \citet[Sec.~1.2]{trepreau2006algebrisation}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Abelian relations of a web
notes: The first integrals are displayed as \(u_1,\ldots,u_n\), but the equation is \(\sum_{i=1}^d f_i(u_i)du_i=0\). The coefficients depend on the corresponding first integral.
statement: An abelian relation of a regular holomorphic \(d\)-web is a \(d\)-tuple of closed one-forms \((\eta_i)\), each annihilating the tangent spaces of the \(i\)-th foliation, with \(\sum_i\eta_i=0\). Locally \(\eta_i=f_i(u_i)du_i\); equivalently \(\eta_i=z_i\,du_i\) with \(dz_i\wedge du_i=0\). This definition is invariant under changing the first integral of each foliation.
reconstruction: The terminal subscript in the list of first integrals is corrected from \(n\) to \(d\). The definition is a tuple of forms; distinct coefficient tuples can sum to the same zero form and must not be identified.
fate: Already used in \citet[Sec.~2]{beauville1980tissus}; precise equivalent equations are \citet[Sec.~1.1, Eqs.~(1)--(2)]{trepreau2006algebrisation}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Rank means dimension over the constants
notes: Rank is the maximum number of linearly independent abelian equations satisfied by the web.
statement: The rank is the complex dimension of the vector space of germs of abelian relations, with linear dependence over constant scalars. It is not the pointwise rank of the cotangent vectors or dimension over the ring of holomorphic functions. In the regular category this dimension is finite, bounded by the number in item 1978-460.9.
reconstruction: The scalar field and the germ interpretation supply the intended meaning of linear independence.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2]{beauville1980tissus} specifies independence over constants, before the April session.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The rank of an algebraic curve web is its genus
notes: Proposition 1: the rank of the web constructed from a curve of genus \(g\) equals \(g\).
statement: For the regular dual web of a smooth irreducible nondegenerate complex projective curve \(C\), the trace map \(\omega\mapsto(p_i^*\omega)_{i=1}^d\) identifies \(H^0(C,\Omega_C^1)\) with its abelian-relation space. Abel's theorem gives \(\sum_i p_i^*\omega=0\), and the converse recovers every relation. Consequently the rank is \(g(C)\). For singular curves, a corresponding assertion uses the appropriate regular dualizing differentials and arithmetic genus; the genus of the normalization cannot simply be substituted.
reconstruction: The smooth scope is the complete statement asserted here; the singular caveat explains why the notebook's unrestricted word ``genus'' is insufficient.
fate: \citet[Sec.~2, pp.~105--106]{beauville1980tissus} states the trace identification. \citet[Sec.~1.2]{trepreau2006algebrisation} explicitly identifies the arithmetic-genus version.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: The Chern rank bound and Castelnuovo number
notes: For an arbitrary \(d\)-web in dimension \(n\), rank \(\le\pi(n,d)\). The notes define \(\pi\) as the maximum genus of a degree-\(d\) curve in \(\mathbb P^n\) and give \(\pi=m(d-1-\tfrac12(m+1)(n-1))\), \(m=\lfloor(d-1)/(n-1)\rfloor\).
statement: For a regular holomorphic codimension-one \(d\)-web in dimension \(n\ge2\), \[\operatorname{rank}\mathcal W\le\pi(n,d)=\sum_{q\ge1}\max\{d-1-q(n-1),0\}.\] This is exactly the notebook's integer formula, including the case where the last summand is zero. For \(d\ge n\), it is also the sharp Castelnuovo bound on the genus of smooth irreducible nondegenerate degree-\(d\) projective curves. The adjective nondegenerate is essential: plane curves embedded in higher projective spaces do not obey the claimed smaller genus bound.
reconstruction: Codimension one, regular general position and nondegeneracy are supplied. The uncertain historical year ``193?'' is not silently made exact. For \(d<n\) the sum still defines the web bound, but no nondegenerate degree-\(d\) curve in \(\mathbb P^n\) is implied.
fate: The bound is classical and is presented in \citet[Sec.~4]{beauville1980tissus}. A proof via independent jets and powers of conormal linear forms is given in \citet[Sec.~2.2, Eqs.~(6)--(8)]{trepreau2006algebrisation}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: Maximal rank implies algebraization: the later repair of the main theorem
notes: The main theorem says: if \(n\ge3\), \(d\ge2n\), and rank is \(\pi(n,d)\), the web can be linearized and extends to a web from \(X\subset\mathbb P^n\). The precise reference is Jahresbericht DMV 80 (1978), 13--110.
statement: Let \(\mathcal W\) be a germ of a regular holomorphic codimension-one \(d\)-web on \(\mathbb C^n\), with every set of at most \(n\) defining conormals independent, \(n\ge3\), \(d\ge2n\), and \(\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal A(\mathcal W)=\pi(n,d)\). Then a local biholomorphism identifies \(\mathcal W\) with the web dual to a degree-\(d\) projective algebraic curve. In particular its leaves become hyperplane pieces. ``Extends'' means this local algebraic identification, not an assertion about the original web's arbitrary global domain.
reconstruction: The analytic category, general position and local interpretation are restored. The theorem is now true, but its attribution as an already completely proved 1978 result requires correction.
fate: The notebook identifies \citet{cherngriffiths1978abel} exactly. \citet[p.~78]{cherngriffiths1981corrections} acknowledges incorrect divisibility lemmas and a separate gap in Eq.~(4.34), retaining the theorem with an extra normality condition defined on p.~79. The unrestricted result is \citet[Theorem~1.1, preprint p.~3]{trepreau2006algebrisation}: first publicly posted 4 August 2005, published 2006. Theorem~2.4, preprint p.~8, even needs only \(2d-3n+1\) abelian relations with independent first jets. The cases \(n=3\) and \(d=2n\) were classical; the new general range is \(n\ge4,d\ge2n+1\). Beauville's February 1979 lecture repeats the then accepted claim and does not repair the later-discovered gap.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: solved in this exact range by Tr'epreau. No open maximal-rank question is asserted here for the omitted planar or small-degree ranges.

title: The projective-connection strategy and its historical limitation
notes: After the main theorem the notes say that a geometry of projective connections is being developed, with an underlining arrow.
statement: This identifies the connection-based strategy for linearization in the Chern--Griffiths work. The notes specify no connection coefficients, curvature equations, or additional independent theorem. In the later proof, abelian relations construct a projective map whose image must be a surface; proving its differential has rank two is the decisive step.
reconstruction: The description of the later rank-two argument is a literature explanation, not a reconstruction of an unrecorded notebook proof. The vague method line cannot validate the original proof's missing step.
fate: Compare the contemporary exposition \citet[Sec.~6]{beauville1980tissus}, the explicit limitations in \citet[p.~78]{cherngriffiths1981corrections}, and \citet[Sec.~1.3, pp.~3--4]{trepreau2006algebrisation}, who separates the standard strategy from his direct calculation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: established in the stated scope; this passage poses no additional open question.

title: A vertex tensor for an arrangement of lines
notes: A. Zamolodchikov introduces \(S_{ij}^{k\ell}(\lambda)\), colors \(1,\ldots,N\), and \(L\) lines with ordered angles \(\lambda_a\). Put a matrix at each crossing, sum over interior-edge colors and leave endpoint colors free. Pairing equal initial and final colors gives \(Z(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_L)\).
statement: Fix a finite oriented line arrangement without triple crossings, an \(N\)-dimensional vector space \(V\), and a matrix function \(R(u)\in\operatorname{End}(V\otimes V)\). At a crossing of lines \(a,b\), use \(R(\lambda_a-\lambda_b)\) in a fixed input/output convention. Contract all internal indices to obtain a boundary tensor, or a matrix on the endpoint state spaces when their orientations permit. Closing corresponding boundary indices and summing gives a trace partition function. This finite algebraic construction does not itself require positivity, convergence, or the Yang--Baxter identity.
reconstruction: The notes' angle is treated as a spectral parameter; physical relativistic rapidity is a separate interpretation. Endpoint ordering and matrix convention are made explicit because they affect whether permutations are absorbed into \(R\).

title: The unspecified large-system asymptotic and boundary independence
notes: Problem 1 asks for the behavior as \(L\to\infty\), with \(\log Z\) proportional to the number of nodes. P000840 writes \(\log Z_i^j\sim L^2\), even without associativity, and says the leading asymptotic is independent of boundary indices.
statement: As a statement about arbitrary crossing matrices, the claimed nonzero quadratic growth and unrestricted boundary independence are false. Take \(R(u)=I_{V\otimes V}\) and order endpoints by the lines they belong to. Every compatible fixed-boundary matrix entry is \(1\), incompatible entries are \(0\), and the trace is \(N^L\). Thus the compatible logarithm is zero, the other logarithm is undefined, and the trace logarithm is \(L\log N\), despite \(\binom L2\) crossings and the Yang--Baxter identity. A meaningful bulk limit needs a specified family of weights, normalization, rapidity distribution, thermodynamic sequence, and allowed boundary conditions.
reconstruction: The counterexample checks the literal quantifiers, not the truth of a particular integrable model. The notes provide no exact asymptotic function or error estimate that could be indexed as a definite unresolved research problem.
fate: \citet[Secs.~2.2, 10.17, 11.2 and 11.4]{baxter1982exactly} analyzes thermodynamic limits for specified models and qualifications on boundary vectors. Those results do not prove the unrestricted statement. Searches for the precise angle-dependent arbitrary-matrix claim produced no exact match; the identity example settles its literal reading.

title: The three-line move is the Yang--Baxter identity
notes: \ru{Ассоциат.}: the tensor does not depend on the mutual disposition of the lines; it suffices to check a pictured equality for three lines.
statement: In the unpermuted tensor-factor convention, the spectral-parameter relation is \[R_{12}(u)R_{13}(u+v)R_{23}(v)=R_{23}(v)R_{13}(u+v)R_{12}(u).\] This equality is precisely invariance under moving one pairwise crossing past the third line, with the same six external indices. Inserting the equality into a larger contraction preserves its boundary tensor. Hence any sequence of such local moves and exchanges of disjoint crossings leaves that tensor unchanged. Changing endpoints, crossing counts, or allowing a pair creation/deletion requires additional identities.

fate: \citet[Sec.~2, Eqs.~(2.5)--(2.6)]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on} derives the factorization equations from associativity; \citet[Sec.~11.1, Eq.~(11.1.6); Sec.~11.2]{baxter1982exactly} proves the lattice move by contraction.

title: The proposed pairwise formula for the leading free energy

title: Factorized scattering and Boltzmann-weight interpretations
notes: Particles move along straight lines, preserving velocities but changing color at collisions; the whole tensor is an \(S\)-matrix. Alternatively it is a statistical sum, with weights described as exponentials of a potential and followed by \ru{вероятности?}.
statement: A two-dimensional elastic factorized-scattering interpretation assigns a conserved rapidity to each particle and an internal-state space to each line; two-body matrices change internal states, and consistency of different collision orders requires the Yang--Baxter identity. Unitarity, crossing and appropriate analyticity are further physical conditions. A classical lattice interpretation instead assigns nonnegative weights \(w=e^{-\beta E}\) to local configurations and sums products. These weights are not probabilities until a normalization is supplied, and a complex scattering amplitude is not generally a Boltzmann weight.
reconstruction: The two interpretations are separated, and ``exponential of the potential'' is normalized in the usual sign convention without treating the tentative probability gloss as a theorem.
fate: The physical assumptions and their independent roles are explicit in \citet[Sec.~2, Eqs.~(2.1)--(2.6)]{zamolodchikovzamolodchikov1978on}.

title: Face spins and a nearest-neighbor partition function
notes: Spins lie in the polygons cut out by the lines and interact with nearest neighbors. The notes write \(H=\sum h(\sigma_A,\sigma_B)\) and \(Z=\sum_{\{\sigma\}}e^{-\beta H}\).
statement: For a finite planar cell decomposition, assign a spin from a finite set to each face and an interaction \(h_e(\sigma_A,\sigma_B)\) to each edge separating adjacent faces. With specified exterior/boundary spins, \(H(\sigma)=\sum_e h_e(\sigma_A,\sigma_B)\) and \(Z=\sum_{\sigma\text{ allowed}}e^{-\beta H(\sigma)}\). For real finite energies and real \(\beta\), this is a finite positive partition function. A representation as local vertex tensors requires a stated encoding of the spin differences/products and the appropriate global constraints.

fate: The face-spin/vertex correspondence is exhibited in \citet[Secs.~10.3 and 11.5]{baxter1982exactly}; the Ising case below is checked directly from the notebook's formula.

title: The displayed Ising vertex weight and its parity constraint
notes: For Ising, \(S_{ij}^{k\ell}=\tfrac12(ijk\ell+1)\exp[-\tfrac\beta2(i+j+k+\ell)]\). The diagram places spin variables in the faces.
statement: Take \(i,j,k,\ell\in\{\pm1\}\) as successive products of the four face spins around a crossing. Their product is one. The prefactor is precisely the indicator of this even-parity condition; the exponential assigns half of the edge energy \(s_e\) at each incident vertex. Multiplying vertex weights therefore gives \(e^{-\beta\sum_e s_e}\) on interior edges, with boundary half-weights completed separately. On a simply connected connected face complex, the parity constraints recover face spins up to a simultaneous sign flip; on a torus they must be supplemented by trivial cycle products to recover periodic spins. Hence the spin partition function differs by the global twofold multiplicity when all spins, including a reference spin, are summed.
reconstruction: The edge-product convention, boundary factors and topology are reconstructed. With the notebook's minus sign, the interaction is \(+\sum_e\sigma_A\sigma_B\); changing to the usual ferromagnetic \(-J\sum_e\sigma_A\sigma_B\) changes the exponential accordingly. No spectral parameter appears in this displayed weight, so it does not prove a Yang--Baxter family for arbitrary angles.
fate: The parity and face-spin correspondence are discussed in \citet[Secs.~10.3 and 11.5, especially p.~287]{baxter1982exactly}. The exact normalization written here is verified by direct multiplication and exhaustive enumeration of the sixteen four-spin assignments in the supplied check code.
